**Even where a table enum IS reachable, only static-Java can lower it — so the normative oracle structurally cannot observe `ValueNotConsistent` (source, 2026-07-25).** Three facts compose: **(1)** the grammar's mixed value-list production has exactly one condition name — `fieldAndValueListConditionName: 'WertNichtKonsistent'` — and its sole creator (`FieldAndValueListConditionCreator`) *always* populates the mixed list (`new EntityListAndValueListConditionImpl(name, ids, null, null, mixedList)`), so **every** parsed `ValueNotConsistent` becomes the `EntityListAndValueConditionMixedList` codegen bean (the string/field-list beans belong to the sibling `feldListeUndWerteListenBedingung` family instead); **(2)** codegen resolves a template by `getClass().getSimpleName()` within the dialect's own dir (`STParameterClassBase`), and `conditionsDir/EntityListAndValueConditionMixedList.st` **exists only under `validation/java`** — as does `operationsDir/ConsistentValueOp.st` (the dynamic-enum value op, emitting `controller.getUiXmlValuesForTableEnum(…)` via `CodeGenDynamicEnumerationBuilder`); **(3)** this is not an accidental gap but a **declared, diagnosed restriction** — `NoMetaModelChecks.checkEnumTables()` rejects any table-enum field for `GROOVY` and `JAVA_SCRIPT_VK` with `MVK_TABLE_ENUMS_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE`. **Consequence — and the correction that matters (a12-kernel-lean, 2026-07-25; verified here): the region has NO witness on ANY dialect, so "static-Java is the only witness" was too generous.** The ADO accessor `IEnumerationType.getTableName()` is abstract and its **sole implementor** — `kernel-md-model`'s `EnumerationTypeImpl` — returns `Optional.empty()` unconditionally (as does `getColumnName()`), and the md public API has no table concept at all. So `getTableName().isPresent()` is never true: the Groovy/JS rejection `MVK_TABLE_ENUMS_NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE` can never fire, the java-only `ConsistentValueOp`/`MixedList` templates are never instantiated, and `RuntimeController.wertNichtKonsistentML` is unreachable. The static-Java lowering *capability* is real but **dead**; there is no witness to promote, so no doctrine exception is needed — the region is simply unreachable at 30.8.1 (a12-kernel-lean reports the same at 31.1.0, and voided its EXP-2026-07-25-02 on that basis rather than conceding a region). The front-end-reach scoping above stands unchanged; only the witness claim needed narrowing. *(Source-read; the template asymmetry was the candidate and the check code + error code is the independent confirmation — the template-layer routing rule, DOC-DISCIPLINE §1. Not probe-locked: unreachable from any authorable fixture.)* **Re-verified 2026-07-25 with anchored `build/` exclusions**, because the whole claim rests on two completeness searches an unanchored exclusion would silently break (trap (3), DOC-DISCIPLINE §1): `getTableName()` has exactly **one** implementor of `IEnumerationType` — `kernel-md-model`'s `EnumerationTypeImpl`, returning `Optional.empty()` unconditionally (the other hits are callers, or `CodeGenEnumerationTypeImpl`/`CodeGenTableCompressed`, unrelated hierarchies) — and **no serialized `tableName`/`columnName` property exists** anywhere in md, so there is no DM-JSON key to author one. `getDependentColumns()` returns `Collections.emptyList()` on that same sole implementor, which kills the dependent-column cascade independently of the table name.

## Header `modelVersion` compatibility — same-major and not-newer than the kernel's model-format (probed 2026-06-12) <a id="kf70"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — a model-header compatibility policy (structure/versioning), outside the evaluation scope.

The kernel polices a document's `header.modelVersion` during `checkConsistency` (not at parse): a mismatch surfaces as a **`KERNEL` ERROR** — `"Version mismatch: Document model version is <X> and application version is <28.4.0>"` — so the model is reported `valid:false` (it loads enough to validate; this is a consistency diagnostic, not a load crash). The "application version" is the **model-format version the running kernel implements** (`30.8.1` implements `28.4.0`). Probed band (against `order-ruled`, app-format `28.4.0`):

| `header.modelVersion` | verdict | rule |
|---|---|---|
| `28.4.0` | valid | exact |
| `28.0.0` | **valid** | same major, **≤** app-format → backward-compatible |
| `28.4.1`, `28.5.0`, `28.9.0` | invalid | same major but **newer** than app-format |
| `27.0.0`, `29.0.0`, `30.8.1` | invalid | different major |

So the kernel is **tolerant of an older same-major model and fail-fast on a newer/different-major one**, with a clear message — exactly the posture we want, enforced upstream. rulekit only *classifies* this verdict (it does not re-derive the rule): the un-coded kernel ERROR is enriched to **`RK_MODEL_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE`** (+ a fix), and an accepted-but-off-reference model gets a tolerant INFO **`RK_MODEL_VERSION_SKEW`**. The reference is `core.ModelFormat.VERSION` (`28.4.0`), bumped in lockstep with the kernel pin (KERNEL-UPGRADE). *(Locked: `cli.ModelVersionPolicyTest` — the band's tolerant/exact/fail-fast cases + the message pattern via `validate.ModelVersion.isVersionMismatch`; the no-implicit-bump round-trip is in the same test.)*

## §1/§3 supplement — value-vs-omission typing is DIRECTIONAL and sign-aware (source + runtime, 2026-06-23) <a id="kf71"></a>

> Fold: folded → §12.

A fired comparison is an OMISSION error (`TRUE_AF`) only when filling an operand **in the breaking direction** could clear it (`BedingungsOperatorHelper.vergleiche`): `GT`/`GE` → `left.kannKleinerWerden || right.kannGroesserWerden`; `LT`/`LE` → the mirror; `EQ` → any operand can move; `NE` → directional on which side is larger (`getFehlerFuerNE`). The per-operand fillability of an **empty number** is asymmetric: `kannGroesserWerden = true` (always fillable larger) but **`kannKleinerWerden = hatVorzeichen`** — fillable smaller only if the field is **signed** (`RuntimeController.feldWertAlsZahl`, TS twin `BigDecimalUtils.makeDecimalFromNonEmptyString`).

- **The sign trigger is `NumberType.positivesOnly`, NOT `minValue`** (the trap): a field with `minValue:1` is still *signed* (probed — `[BirthDay] >= 0` empty types OMISSION); only `positivesOnly:true` makes it unsigned (`[StockOnHand:positivesOnly] >= 0` empty types **VALUE**). `minValue` is a range constraint, independent of `hatVorzeichen`.
- Consequence: `[Unsigned] >= 0` (empty) is a **VALUE** error — an unsigned 0 can't shrink, so no fill breaks `>= 0`; the same over a *signed* field is **OMISSION**. Both `<= X` are OMISSION (filling larger breaks them).

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DirectionalPolarityDiffTest` (unsigned `StockOnHand` vs signed `Quantity`); the signed cases also in `adapter.laws.PolarityDiffTest`/`AggPolarityDiffTest`; the **`NE` directional arm** (`getFehlerFuerNE` — previously documented here but never `!=`-directionally DiffTest-exercised) is **corpus-locked** since 2026-07-17 by the portable `empty-polarity` cases (signedness + literal-direction + filled-state pairs, tri-engine replay incl. the JS oracle). The interpreter's directional treatment: INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF9.)*

**Function-operand fillability — `CurrentRepetition` and `FirstFilledValue` (probe + full-message fuzz, 2026-06-24).** The directional fillability above extends to value FUNCTIONS, not just fields/aggregates — and the naive "any empty/short star tail ⇒ fillable" over-reports OMISSION for two:

- **`CurrentRepetition(group)`** is the structural **row index**; no field-fill changes it, so a fired comparison against it is **always VALUE** (probed: `CurrentRepetition(Lines) > 2` on row 3 → VALUE). The generic fallback wrongly reads its group argument as an "unfilled field" and types it OMISSION.
- **`FirstFilledValue(g*/f)`** is **OMISSION iff NO row is filled** (the empty selection folds to the kind's fillable not-given value — the 2026-07-08 refinement below) **or an instantiated EMPTY row PRECEDES the first filled one** — filling that (earlier / any) row could become the new first value and clear the error — else **VALUE** (the first value is fixed; *later* empties are irrelevant). Probed: `(empty, 60)` → OMISSION; `(60, empty)` and `(60)` → VALUE.

The naive star-omission notion (`starOmission`: any empty cell / short tail) is too broad for `FirstFilledValue` — only an empty/filter marker reached before the terminal value matters. Both were mis-typed OMISSION until the **harness-D full-message fuzz** caught them (117/200 seeds — invisible to the codes-only gate). *(Locked: `adapter.laws.FullMessageFuzzDiffTest` + `CurrentRepetitionDiffTest`/`FirstFilledValueDiffTest`/`FirstFilledValueFilterEncounterDiffTest`, now asserting polarity, not just firing; interpreter `firstFilledScan` + `funcFill`.)*

**A no-row first star DOES taint a later operand's value — the source-level "omitted tail" clause does not manifest at runtime (differential vs. dynamic-Groovy, 2026-07-22).** In a multi-operand `FirstFilledValue(star, …, fallback)`, a first `star` that visits **no concrete cell** — an uninstantiated group (flat `Parcels*/Weight` with zero rows), or an instantiated parent with an empty child repetition (nested `Parcels*/Segments*/Load` where a parcel row has zero segments) — reads as a **not-given prefix**: `RuntimeController.combineFeldListe` reaches the star's repetitions and `addValue`s a not-given cell, so `FirstValueCombiner.notGivenFieldBeforeFirstGiven` is set and a fired later-fallback comparison types **OMISSION**, not VALUE. Reading `FirstValueCombiner.getValue` alone predicts the opposite — its `(value == null) && omittedTail` clause would let an omitted tail *not* taint a selected value — but that clause only decides the **all-exhausted identity**; whenever the star is actually reached, the not-given cell taints first, independent of `omittedTail`. The interpreter's `firstFilledScan` marks the no-row star fillable (`if (!visitedRow) fillable = true`), matching the kernel. This **refutes** a12-kernel-lean **SPEC-2026-07-22-06** (which requested the interpreter type such a firing VALUE); an empirical sweep found no document shape where dynamic-Groovy yields VALUE for a fallback selected after a no-row first star, and applying the requested change makes the interpreter diverge. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueOmittedTailDiffTest` — flat + nested no-row star, instantiated-empty prefix, and a star-selects-value VALUE control, all matching the kernel.)*

**`FirstFilledValue` over an EMPTY selection returns its operand kind's OWN not-given value — number → the fillable 0, else NOT-GIVEN (source + differential 2026-07-08; full kind matrix 2026-08-02).** The kernel's `FirstValueCombiner` is a per-kind family — `FirstValueCombinerNumber`/`Date`/`DateRange`/`String` — and on an empty selection (no filled cell) each returns its own `notGivenValue()`: `NICHT_ANGEGEBENE_ZAHL` for NUMBER (a *value*, the fillable `0` — the empty-as-0 its Sum/Min/Max siblings give), but the owner-kind NOT-GIVEN value for every other admitted kind. Observable: a Boolean, custom, string/enumeration, date/date-fragment, time, date-time, or date-range `FirstFilledValue(empty)` in a comparison does **not** fire, and a computation into that target is **CLEARED**; only a NUMBER empty `FirstFilledValue` yields the fillable 0. So the kind-following `FirstFilledValue` identity is not uniformly numeric. *(Interpreter: `firstFilledValue`'s empty identity is `Val.Num(0)` iff the operand kind is NUMBER, else `Val.Unknown`; before the fix an unconditional `Num(0)` crashed `ValCompare` against the real value. Locked branch-for-branch by `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueKindDiffTest`, `FirstFilledValueAdditionalKindDiffTest`, and the catalog aggregate-identity probes; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF83.)*

**…and the kinds that may SHARE one `FirstFilledValue` operand list are not the two families we published — `DATE` and `DATE_FRAGMENT` are NOT interchangeable (measured 2026-08-15).** Our operator catalog carried, as a `constraints` line served by `dmtool operators FirstFilledValue`, that "STRING/CUSTOM/ENUMERATION or DATE/DATE_FRAGMENT are compatible families". The string half holds — `STRING`+`ENUMERATION`, `STRING`+`CUSTOM` and `ENUMERATION`+`CUSTOM` are all ACCEPTED. **The date half is wrong, though not as first recorded — corrected 2026-08-15 the same day.** This entry first read "`DATE` and `DATE_FRAGMENT` are NOT interchangeable", from a row comparing a `yyyy-MM-dd` Date against a `yyyy-MM` DateFragment. That varies the KIND and the DECLARED FORMAT together and cannot say which was refused — the same confound class a12-kernel-lean had just caught in the group-operand rows, reproduced inside the reply correcting it. Separated, the conclusion inverts: **the temporal gate reads the declared format, not the kind.** A Date declared `yyyy` beside a DateFragment declared `yyyy` is **ADMITTED across two kinds**; two Dates differing only in declared format are **REFUSED** (`MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`). This is the same rule `FieldValuesNotUniqueAdmissionLawsTest` had already locked for its own carrier against the same discriminating pair — so the carriers AGREE, and any "compatible families" table phrased in kinds is wrong on both. Cross-family (`STRING`+`NUMBER`, `DATE`+`STRING`) draws the same code; a `Confirm` operand keeps its own `MVK_NO_BOOLY_ALLOWED`, so the varying-types code is not a catch-all. **The trap for a consumer** is that a date-fragment's *comparability* partition is a DIFFERENT gate and it is easy to mistake one for the other: a yearless fragment (`MM`) cannot compare to a full date at all (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`) regardless of any operand list. This was published prose rather than a measured row until a12-kernel-lean pointed out that our "FirstFilledValue is closed" claim covered admission only.

**…and the rule GENERALIZES — it is confirmed on a second kind pair that shares one declared format (measured 2026-08-15, same day).** `DATE`+`DATE_FRAGMENT` is the closest pair in the family (a fragment *is* a partial date), so on its own it leaves open whether the kernel simply treats those two as one type. The independent witness is `TIME` + `DATE_TIME`, which no one would call one type, and which can be made to share a format string **exactly** because a `DATE_TIME` may be declared with the degenerate time-only `HH:mm:ss` (§6, probe-enumerated 2026-06-26). Both discriminating rows behave as the format rule predicts: a `TIME HH:mm:ss` beside a `DATE_TIME HH:mm:ss` is **ADMITTED across two kinds**, while a `DATE_TIME` at ISO beside a `DATE_TIME` at `HH:mm:ss` — **one kind, two formats** — is **REFUSED** `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`. Both same-kind, same-format controls admit, and every operand also appears alone against the same comparison. So the gate reads the declared format across the temporal family, not merely within the date/fragment neighbourhood.

**The bound this paragraph first asserted was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the finding.** It read "`TIME` and `DATE_TIME` each admit exactly ONE declared format, so the discrimination is unauthorable outside the `DATE`/`DATE_FRAGMENT` pair; the rule is vacuous, not false, elsewhere." That is a **completeness claim drawn from a sample** — six `TIME` and five `DATE_TIME` candidates probed, one acceptance seen in each — and the sample missed a legal value that **this repository had already enumerated in §6 fourteen weeks earlier**. Consulting the existing enumeration would have cost one search and would have inverted the conclusion, which is the whole point of the claim-kind rule: absence needs an enumeration you can show, never a handful of tries. Two smaller traps rode along: an earlier draft of the sibling rows authored `HH:mm` and `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm` — **both illegal formats** — so those rows measured model invalidity rather than the gate, and `DATE_RANGE` was omitted from a claim phrased over the whole family — **that omission is closed the same day**: a range's allowlisted **(format, separator) PAIR** gives it two legal declarations too, and both rows behave like the rest of the family (same pair ACCEPT, two legal pairs `MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`, and a range beside a DATE likewise), so the claim now covers every temporal kind rather than the four that happened to be measured.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.FirstFilledValueFamilyLawsTest` — every row a complete emitted code list, each refusal paired with its homogeneous control; `theLegalFormatSetPerTemporalKindIsAWhitelist`, `theFormatKeyingHoldsOnASecondKindPairSharingOneFormat` and `theFormatKeyingCoversDateRangeToo` carry the family coverage. Catalog corrected in the same change.)*

**Fill propagates through ARITHMETIC — an empty operand keeps the result fillable (source `VkBigDecimal`, differential 2026-07-07; aggregate correction 2026-07-21).** The directional fill (`kannGroesserWerden`/`kannKleinerWerden`) is a property of the *value*, and every arithmetic operation carries it forward, so `[F] != [A] + [B]` with `B` an empty (fillable) field types the fired comparison **OMISSION** (the RHS can still grow) — not VALUE. Each op propagates differently (`VkBigDecimal.add`/`subtract`/`multiply`/`divide`/`power`): `+` combines both directions; `−` **flips the subtrahend** (`a−b` grows if `a` grows or `b` shrinks); `×`/`÷` are **SIGN-DEPENDENT** (`produktKannGroesser/KleinerWerden` — a factor pushes the product up by growing when the other factor is positive / shrinking when it is negative; `÷` is `a × (1/b)`); `^` follows `powCanChange` (base magnitude vs 0/1/−1 and exponent parity). This rides the SAME runtime `VkBigDecimal` in both strategies (codegen emits calls to it) ⟹ codegen-parity. **The VALUE FUNCTIONS carry the flags too**, each via its own `VkBigDecimal` op: `setScale` (the `Round*` family) **PRESERVES** them exactly; `abs` **TRANSFORMS** them with the value sign (`g'=g∨s`, `s'=(pos∧s)∨(neg∧g)` — `|x|` grows off either direction, shrinks only toward 0); `min`/`max` (operand-list `Min`/`Max`) **COMBINE** directionally (min shrinks via either operand, grows via the smaller; max mirrors); `bereichAlsZahl` (`RangeAsNumber`) is **GROW-ONLY** (`kannKleiner=false`, value ≥ 0). So `RoundAccounting(<fillable arith>, n)` / `AbsValue(…)` / `Min(…)` / `RangeAsNumber(…)` are likewise fillable. **NUMBER aggregate fill has two stages** (`NumberCombiner`): before any present value, `Sum`/`MaxValue`/`MinValue` expose the zero identity with both directions; afterward, `Sum` grows and shrinks exactly when a missing contributing declaration is signed, `MaxValue` is grow-only, and `MinValue` shrink-only. The earlier unsigned-all-empty VALUE claim conflated those stages and is superseded. *(Locked: `AggDirectionalPolarityDiffTest` + `NumericAggregatePolarityDiffTest`; interpreter `funcFill`, INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF9/IF200.)* *(Interpreter treatment IF69 for arithmetic + IF71 for the value functions: `ArithFill` + `Interpreter.fill(Expr.Arith)`/`funcFill`; differential-locked `adapter.laws.ArithmeticFillPolarityDiffTest`/`FunctionFillPolarityDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter.ArithmeticFillTest`/`FunctionFillTest`.)*

**Arithmetic fill is executable, not merely “sign-dependent/parity” (source-completed + dual-route discriminator 2026-07-20).** With `(g,s)` = can-grow/can-shrink, addition is `(a.g∨b.g, a.s∨b.s)` and subtraction is `(a.g∨b.s, a.s∨b.g)`. Multiplication grow is `(a.g∧b.g) ∨ (a.s∧b.s) ∨ (b>0∧a.g) ∨ (b<0∧a.s) ∨ (a>0∧b.g) ∨ (a<0∧b.s)`; shrink is `(a.g∧b.s) ∨ (a.s∧b.g) ∨ (b>0∧a.s) ∨ (b<0∧a.g) ∨ (a>0∧b.s) ∨ (a<0∧b.g)`. The joint terms survive when both current signs are zero. Division first rejects current zero, then multiplies by reciprocal fill `(b.s∨(b<0∧b.g), b.g∨(b>0∧b.s))`. Power is deliberately conservative: negative exponents recurse through reciprocal-first staging; fixed exponent, fixed base, and both-variable branches split around exponent zero, base `−1/0/1`, and parity; only the both-variable `base>1`/neither-shrink case is grow-only, otherwise it may return both directions. This is policy rather than exact reachable-set analysis: with the same `0^0` value, `0 ^ empty-unsigned > 0` fires OMISSION while `0 ^ empty-signed > 0` fires VALUE in both kernel strategies. Quiet-invalid power domains never reach comparison typing as an ordinary fixed value, and fractional exponents are rejected during authoring. *(Locked: `ArithmeticFillPolarityDiffTest` zero-base tri-check + multiplatform `ArithmeticFillBranchTest` full branch matrix.)*

## §5 supplement — tolerance boundary + comparison rescaling (runtime, 2026-06-10, RT-semantics drain) <a id="kf72"></a>

> Fold: folded → §5.

- **`DiffersWithToleranceRange{N}` fires strictly beyond the tolerance**: satisfied iff `|R₁₉(a) − R₁₉(b)| > N` after independently normalizing both operands — a difference of *exactly* N is still within tolerance and does **not** fire, in either direction. The boundary and normalization order are the traps. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.ToleranceComparisonLawsTest` + `ToleranceExactnessDiffTest`.)*
- **Source-read precision policy** (`VkBigDecimal`): a NUMBER **comparison** rescales both operands to scale 19 `HALF_UP` before comparing — and this is **`BedingungsOperatorHelper.vergleiche` (lines 164-167), not `VkBigDecimal.compareTo`** (which is plain): so the rescale applies to **all** comparison ops `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`/`==`/`!=`, but **NOT to `min`/`max` selection**, which the kernel does at full precision via `VkBigDecimal.compareTo` (`SummeCombiner`/`MinWertCombiner` etc.). Separately, **every arithmetic operation `+`/`−`/`×`/`÷`/`^` rounds to `MathContext(50)` `HALF_UP`** (`INTERNAL_PRECISION`). `Sum` therefore starts at zero and left-folds the resolved encounter stream, rounding after every present addition; model declaration order for group expansion and row order for repetitions are semantic, so sorting, reassociation, exact accumulation followed by one rounding, and parallel reduction are invalid. Missing contributors perform no arithmetic step but retain their own declaration for polarity. The kernel team's note was "no legal model surfaces the scale-19 rounding (field scales cap far below 19)" — but arithmetic expressions can exceed it, so the rounding is observable. **Interpreter status: reproduced in full.** The comparison scale-19 rounding rides `Dec.scale19` (comparison ops only — `min`/`max` stay full-precision), every `Dec` arithmetic operation takes the same context on JVM and Node, and aggregate group expansion preserves declaration order. `DecimalPrecisionParityDiffTest` tri-checks observable addition, subtraction, division, positive-power, and reciprocal-first negative-power discriminators against Groovy-dynamic and generated Java; `DecimalHostParityTest` and `NumericAggregateSemanticsTest` lock the exact primitive staged/order discriminators on JVM and Node. *(Also locked: `PrecisionDiffTest` — scale-19 comparison; `ArithmeticDiffTest` — multiplication; `DivPowDiffTest` — operator-domain behavior.)*
- **The rounding operators are directional, not truncation** (`BigDecimalUtils`, second drain): after the shared scale-19 `HALF_UP` pre-round, `RoundDown` is **FLOOR** (toward −∞: `RoundDown(−1.4) = −2`), `RoundUp` is **CEILING** (`RoundUp(−1.4) = −1`), and `RoundAccounting` is **HALF_UP** (away from zero on the .5 boundary, both signs). The negative-value behavior is the modeller trap — "down" does not mean "toward zero".
- **Exactly one ordered post-order arithmetic rewrite precedes evaluation.** After visiting its children, each original multiplication pulls only immediate division-root operands. Ordinary factors remain first in authored order; extracted numerators and denominators follow in division encounter order; multi-factor products are left folds; newly created products are not revisited. `a*{b/c}` and `{b/c}*a` both become `{a*b}/c`, but `x*{{a/b}/c}` becomes `{x*{a/b}}/c` and stops. This is not direct authored-tree evaluation, global normalization, or a fixed point. *(Source: `DivisionTransformer` + parse-tree traversal/composite code generation; locked against dynamic-Groovy and generated Java by `adapter.laws.ArithmeticLoweringDiffTest`, with AST shape locked on JVM+JS by `interpreter.ArithmeticLoweringTest`.)*
- **A scale-19 `HALF_UP` pre-rounding precedes every target-scale rounding** — observable with three separate thirds: `RoundDown([q]/3 + [q]/3 + [q]/3, 0) == [q]` fires for `q=1` because the independently precision-50-rounded thirds sum to `1−10⁻⁵⁰`, then pre-round to 1 before the floor. The former multiplied-third example is not a discriminator: the one-pass division rewrite makes that product exact first. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.RoundingLawsTest` + `ArithmeticLoweringDiffTest`.)*
- **Interpreter status: the full `Round*` family is reproduced** — the operand-list `RoundDown`/`RoundUp`/`RoundAccounting([expr][, n])` and their bare-field `*Value(field[, n])` siblings. **The decimal-places argument is OPTIONAL on BOTH forms** (grammar `rundenOperOp`/`rundenOp` — `(',' ZiffernFolge)?`; an absent `n` is the integer round, places 0; kernel-pinned 2026-07-10, IF102 — a real workspace model carries the 1-arg `RoundDown([X])`). `Dec.roundTo(places, mode)` replays `BigDecimalUtils.runden`'s two-step exactly (pre-round to scale 19 HALF_UP, then `setScale(places, FLOOR/CEILING/HALF_UP)`); on JS, big.js has no native FLOOR/CEILING, so they are emulated by sign (away-from-zero for negatives under FLOOR, the mirror for CEILING) — `toward −∞ / +∞`. *(Interpreter-locked: `adapter.laws.RoundDiffTest` — the negative-boundary FLOOR/CEILING + the `.5` HALF_UP catchers, against the live kernel; the cross-platform `interpreter.RoundToTest` re-asserts the values on JS; the fuzz net adds three round rules — `PerfCatalog.fuzz()`.)*

## §2 supplement — patterns skip empties; operand-list `Min`/`Max` do not (runtime, 2026-06-10, RT-semantics drain) <a id="kf73"></a>

> Fold: folded → §2.

Two more edges of the §2 empty-value table (all three now canonical in §2's override table), drained from `RuntimeController` and the `Combiner` contract's `testValidity` flag:

- **An empty string does not violate a pattern** — `PatternViolated` rides the string column (not evaluated on empty; `vergleichePatternSTRING` returns unknown), so it does **not** fire on an absent value. "Empty surely violates my format" is the trap — absence needs `FieldNotFilled`, not a pattern. (A fired pattern comparison is always a *value* error — there is no fillable branch.)
- **The operand-list `Min`/`Max` substitute an empty number as 0; the starred aggregates skip it.** `Min([A], [B])` with `A` empty evaluates `Min(0, B)` — the 0 wins — while `MinValue(G*/F)` ignores unspecified operands (canonical §2). The two list-op families differ exactly on empty handling (the kernel's `EntityListOperations` vs `ListOperOps` split).
- **Value lists and empties, both directions** (third drain): an empty *subject* field is never in any value list (not evaluated, no fire); and an empty *field entry* of a numeric value list can **never be matched** — the empty-as-0 substitution does *not* apply to list entries (`feldWertInWerteListe`: an entry that could still change never equals), so `FieldValueIncludedInValueList(Q, [Allowed])` with `Q = 0` and `Allowed` empty does **not** fire.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.EmptyValueLawsTest` — `emptyStringDoesNotViolateAPattern` / `operandListMinSeesAnEmptyNumberAsZero` / `anEmptyFieldIsNeverInAValueList` / `anEmptyListEntryFieldNeverMatches_noZeroSubstitution`.)*
