### §6 supplement — date ranges are closed intervals: touching ranges overlap (runtime, 2026-06-10, RT-semantics drain) <a id="kf90"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

`DateRangesOverlap` / `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` treat both the start **and** the end day as belonging to the range (`DatumBereich.ueberlappt`: overlap ⇔ `end1 ≥ start2 ∧ end2 ≥ start1`). Consequences, both probe-locked:

- **Back-to-back periods sharing a boundary day overlap** — a window ending 31.01 and a coverage starting 31.01 fire the overlap. Seamless non-overlapping periods must start the day *after* the previous end.
- Adjacent-day ranges (end 31.01, start 01.02) do not overlap; a contained range does.
- Source note: an *inverted* range (start after end) silently never overlaps — defensively handled, though the format tier normally prevents one from existing.

**Historical correction (2026-07-08):** the 2026-06-24 probe correctly established the `IN` syntax and closed-interval scalar-vs-list behavior, but its “semantically identical / shared evaluator / always VALUE” conclusion was false. IF72 above is authoritative: `DateRangesOverlap` is any-pair with a sticky reached-filter flag, while `AtLeastOneDateRangeOverlaps` is scalar-vs-list with matched-container polarity and scalar-first early exit. The grammar distinction remains: value-list operators and `NumberOfValueInFields` use `In`, this overlap predicate uses `IN` (the interpreter accepts the kernel's `In`/`in`/`IN` token variants). *(Locked by `adapter.laws.DateRangeOverlapSemanticsDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter.DateRangeOverlapTest`.)*

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DateRangeOverlapLawsTest`.)*

### §6 supplement — partially-known-date extraction gating + the *FromDate date-time source (source + probe, 2026-06-17) <a id="kf91"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — authoring-tier gating (parse/consistency codes over precision × operator), outside the evaluation scope; the datetime-source acceptance is canonical in §6.

`DayFromDate`/`MonthFromDate`/`YearFromDate`/`QuarterFromDate`, `AddDays`, and `DifferenceInDays` accept a **DateTime** source, not only a Date (kernel date table: "X can be Date or DateTime"); `DifferenceInDays` also accepts mixed date/date-time pairs. `DifferenceInMonths`/`DifferenceInYears` and `AddYears`/`AddMonths` stay Date-only. On a **partially-known date** (a `DateType` carrying a `datePrecision` other than FULL): **`DayFromDate` is rejected outright** — `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE` (probed on a DAY_OPTIONAL field; distinct from `ValueAsDate`'s `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP`) — while `MonthFromDate`/`YearFromDate`/`QuarterFromDate` are **accepted on a DAY_OPTIONAL** date (probed). **The full precision gradient is now source-confirmed and locked** (was BA-stated, IG66→graduated): `DateUtils.checkOperationConsistentToPartialKnown` rejects extracting a component the field's `datePrecision` allows to be unknown, keyed on the fragment (`d`/`m`/`y`). The 4×3 matrix (op × precision, all rejects `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE`): **DayFromDate** — rejected on DAY/MONTH/YEAR_OPTIONAL (never usable on a partial date); **MonthFromDate** & **QuarterFromDate** (Quarter maps to the MONTH component) — accept DAY_OPTIONAL only, reject MONTH/YEAR_OPTIONAL; **YearFromDate** — accepts DAY_OPTIONAL + MONTH_OPTIONAL, rejects YEAR_OPTIONAL. Monotone: a component is extractable iff guaranteed present under the declared optionality (MONTH_OPTIONAL ⇒ day also unknown; YEAR_OPTIONAL ⇒ all unknown), so YEAR_OPTIONAL rejects every extraction. Confirms BA L4123-4125 exactly. **Add\* on a date fragment is gated by the format's granularity** — `AddDays` needs a day, `AddMonths` a month, `AddYears` a year, else **`MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`** (probed: `AddMonths(MM-fragment)` and `AddYears(yyyy-fragment)` accept, `AddDays(MM-fragment)` rejects; BA L4076-4091). **Source:** the extract gating is `CheckDatumExtractOpImpl` → `DateUtils.checkOperationConsistentToPartialKnown` (rejects extracting the field's *optional* component → `MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE`); the Add\* granularity is `CheckDatumAddOpImpl.check` → `DateUtils.checkOperationConsistentToDateFormat`, gated on `format.hasComponent(dateFragment)` → `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`. *(Locked: `validate.laws.DateExtractionLawsTest` + `validate.laws.DateFragmentArithmeticLawsTest` + `adapter.laws.DateFunctionsOverDateTimeDiffTest`.)*

**The `MVK_NO_DATE` operand refusal has an exact owner-backed denominator on both public extraction carriers** (measured 2026-09-01). `YearFromDate` and `DateFromDateTime` each report `MVK_NO_DATE` for NUMBER, STRING, ENUMERATION, BOOLEAN, CONFIRM, DATE_RANGE and CUSTOM fields; the matrix holds the model and error-field guard fixed and moves only the source field. `UNKNOWN` is deliberately outside that statement because it has no authorable A12 counterpart to put through the kernel oracle, so a client may refuse the seven measured kinds and must leave `UNKNOWN` kernel-arbitrated. `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` is the distinct refusal for a temporal source whose **declared format** lacks the component asked for — which is why that code cannot be predicted from the operand's kind ([KF211](#kf211)) and remains delegated (API-FINDINGS 130). *(Locked: `validate.laws.DateExtractionLawsTest.everyRepresentableNonPointKindIsNotADateOnBothCarriers`; typed denominator: `rulekit.dsl.operators.DateExtractionOperandKindTest`.)*

### §6 supplement — Valid/Invalid truth projections are exact complements; full verdict polarity is not derivable (runtime, corrected 2026-07-20) <a id="kf92"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

`Valid(Date(...))` fires only when **all referenced parts are specified AND** they form a real calendar date; `Invalid(Date(...))` fires when the date is impossible (e.g. 31 February) **OR any referenced part is unspecified**. Their strong-Kleene truth projections are exact complements: real → TRUE/FALSE, unreal or incomplete → FALSE/TRUE, malformed → UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN. The non-derivability is at the full verdict level: incomplete makes `Invalid` an OMISSION error, while present-but-unreal makes it VALUE; `Valid` is false in both cases. To fire `Invalid` only on a complete-but-impossible date, prefix `AllFieldsFilled(...)`. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.DateValidityLawsTest` + `DateConstructionDiffTest`.)*

**The BA's "1583 Gregorian floor" (L3833) is NOT a runtime `Date(...)`-construct criterion (probed 2026-06-17, probe-evidence).** `Invalid(Date(1,1,1500))` does **not** fire — the runtime treats `01.01.1500` as a valid constructed date (the same rule fires for an impossible date, so the mechanism works). The floor **is** enforced — at the *value* tier: the later §3 supplement ("a DATE value has an always-on lower bound", 2026-07-09) verified and locked the formal check on stored/computed values (`datumFalsch`, `ComputedDateGregorianFloorDiffTest`). (A 4th BA-vs-source/runtime discrepancy found this review, after `INVALID_INTERVAL`, the semantic-index operator, and the fragment-comparison code.)

### §6 supplement — date-fragment comparability partition (probe-confirmed, 2026-06-17) <a id="kf93"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

Without a base year, two date(-fragment) values compare (`==`/`!=`/ordering) **only if both carry a year or neither does** — a year-bearing fragment/full date and a non-year fragment are incomparable, rejected with **`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`** ("only allowed to compare dates with other fitting dates"). Probed: `[YearOnly:yyyy] == [FullDate]` accepts; `[MonthOnly:MM] == [YearOnly:yyyy]` rejects. **Note the code:** a *direct comparison* gives `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`, **not** the BA's `MVK_DATE_WITH_AND_WITHOUT_YEAR` (that is the `DifferenceIn…`/overlap-op code for mixed-year args). A declared **base year** relaxes the partition (a missing year reads as the base year — BA L4069-4074, not probed here). (Source `CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkDateType` → `DateFormat.formatsConsistentRegardingFormat(fmt1, fmt2, hasBaseYear())`; the same method also fires `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` for a BASE_YEAR vs a non-date-specification operand — confirming the code is this comparison path's, not the `DifferenceIn…` path's.) *(Locked: `validate.laws.DateFragmentComparabilityLawsTest`.)*

**rulekit treatment — a date fragment IS a `DateOperand` (read + author, 2026-07-05).** Because the kernel collapses a fragment to a plain `Date` for parse/check/render/compare, `DateFragmentRef` is a full `DateOperand` (not the earlier "source-only" kind): it compares with all six operators against a date field, another fragment, `Date(...)`, `Today`/`Now`, `Base Year`, or a date expression, rendering as a bare `[field]`. F10 read converts a fragment comparison through the same date machinery — on the left (`fieldValueComparison` `case DATE_FRAGMENT`) and as a right/date operand (`convertDateOperand`, which previously threw `IllegalArgumentException: … is not a date field (kind=DATE_FRAGMENT)` when a fragment sat in a date-operand slot). rulekit does **not** re-enforce the year-class partition on read — the kernel already accepted the rule. *(Locked: `adapter.DateFragmentComparisonReadTest` — kernel-valid + round-trip for fragment-vs-date, date-vs-fragment, and fragment-vs-fragment.)*

**§6 supplement — date-fragment RUNTIME completion: earliest concrete date, base-year for the year (probe-confirmed, 2026-07-07 — canonical §6).** The *evaluation* companion to the comparability partition above (that is the authoring gate; this is what a valid fragment then does at runtime). A `DateFragmentType` value is stored in its `formatOfFragment` (one of `yyyy-MM`, `yyyy`, `MM`, `MM-dd`); when the runtime reads a fragment field for a comparison / `Add*` / extraction it **completes the missing components to the *earliest* concrete date** and compares as a plain `Date`:

- **missing MONTH → `01`, missing DAY → `01`, missing YEAR → the model base year** (`modelInfo.baseYear`, default 2000). Probed by comparing against a full DATE field of a known value: `[CardExpiry:yyyy-MM = "2024-06"] == [Full = "2024-06-01"]` **fires** (not `2024-06-15`); `[WarrantyYear:yyyy = "2024"] == [Full = "2024-01-01"]` fires (not `2024-06-15`); `[SaleWindow:MM-dd = "06-01"] == [BillMonth:MM = "06"]` fires (`MM` completes day → `01`).
- The **base year is observable**: with `modelInfo.baseYear = 2024`, `[BillMonth:MM = "06"] == [Full = "2024-06-01"]` fires but `== "2023-06-01"` does not (the year-less fragment completes its year to the *declared* base year, which is also what makes it comparable to a year-bearing date — the partition's base-year relaxation).
- **Both kernel strategies share the completion** — it lives in `RuntimeController.feldWertAlsDatum` (kernel-core-runtime), and the codegen's `FieldIdOperation` emits `controller.feldWertAlsDatum(idx, …)` for a date field — so runtime and codegen agree by construction (`DateUtil.getValueAsDate` + `PartiallyKnownDatesUtil.replaceMonthAndYearIfUnknown(…, INTERVAL_START)`). A malformed fragment value (bad month, non-numeric) is `datumFormatFalsch` and suppresses the referencing rule, like any date.

*(Interpreter: `DatePrecision.FRAGMENT` + `DateMath.completeFragmentToIso` + `Document.resolveValue`/`FormalError` — IF57. Locked: `adapter.laws.DateFragmentComparisonDiffTest` — the three-way differential incl. the java-static codegen leg — + multiplatform `interpreter.DateFragmentEvalTest`.)*

### §6 supplement — TIME and DATE_TIME value kinds (implemented 2026-06-07) <a id="kf94"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

(The kernel truths — TIME orderable like DATE, DATE_TIME decomposing via the extraction lattice — are canonical in §6/the field-types table; the modeling/treatment log stays.) **`TIME` is orderable exactly like `DATE`** (no scale, no D13 machinery): `[ServiceWindowStart] >= [ServiceWindowEnd]` is kernel-valid (a time field vs another time field). Modeled as `TimeRef`/`TimeOperand`/`TimeExpr`, obtained from `BoundModel.time(path)`; the same six order operators as dates. Time constant literals (`"17:00:00"`) are implemented (family 1, see the §6 supplement above).

**`DATE_TIME` decomposes into its parts and components** — the kernel's `DateExtractionOperationName` covers the whole lattice, and **the extractions accept a `DATE_TIME` source, not only their nominal kind** (verified against the workspace `DateTimeValues_DM` model, where a single `DateTimeType Source` feeds every extraction):

| operator | source kind(s) | result |
|---|---|---|
| `YearFromDate`/`MonthFromDate`/`DayFromDate`/`QuarterFromDate` | DATE **or** DATE_TIME | number |
| `HoursFromTime`/`MinutesFromTime`/`SecondsFromTime` | TIME **or** DATE_TIME | number |
| `DateFromDateTime` | DATE_TIME | date |
| `TimeFromDateTime` | DATE_TIME | time |

rulekit models the numeric ones as `DateExtraction` (kind NUMBER), the part-extractions as `DateTimePart` (kind DATE/TIME), with a common `TemporalOperand` source supertype (`DateOperand`/`TimeOperand`/`DateTimeOperand`). DATE_TIME is both a decomposition source **and** (since family 3) a directly comparable kind — see the construction supplement below. *(Locked: `adapter.TimeAndDateTimeReadTest` — render + kernel-valid + round-trip for TIME ordering, time-of-day extraction, year-from-DATE_TIME, and Date/TimeFromDateTime; N7 catalog examples for all five new operators. The order fixture gained `PickupTime` TimeType + `ScheduledAt` DateTimeType fields; modelkit gained `timeField`/`dateTimeField`.)*

**`Time` / `DateTime` construction + direct DATE_TIME comparison (implemented 2026-06-07, Time arity/extractor domain completed 2026-07-30, family 3).** Two kernel constructors build temporal values from parts: `Time(hour?, minute?, second?)` (DE `Zeit`, the `ITimeConstructionOperation`) → a TIME; and `DateTime(date, time)` (DE keyword is the untranslated `DateTime`, the `IDateTimeConstructionOperation`) → a DATE_TIME. `Time` accepts a zero-to-three-component **prefix**: `Time()` is midnight, `Time("10")` is 10:00:00, `Time("10","30")` is 10:30:00, and the full form supplies seconds; every omitted trailing component defaults to zero. Present-component grammar mirrors `Date(...)`: a component is a bare declaration-compatible field, a quoted constant, or the position-matching `HoursFromTime`/`MinutesFromTime`/`SecondsFromTime` extraction — a bracketed field value `[H]` is a parse error (`MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`). The extraction source is the ordinary nonliteral Time/DateTime expression grammar, so direct fields, shifts, and `Now` are admitted, while a direct temporal literal beneath it is `MVK_NO_CONST`. A quoted Time component has a real-clock range gate but no width gate: `"1"` is accepted as the hour while `"24"` is refused.

**The nested source is evaluated before extraction, and its no-value reason survives to the constructor.** An empty source contributes numeric zero with missing provenance, so an enclosing `Time(...)` is incomplete rather than manufactured midnight. A formally unavailable source stays unavailable. A reached temporal expression that has no value—discriminated by `AddHours(DateTimeField, field / 0)`—contributes fixed zero instead, so `Time(HoursFromTime(theShift))` is midnight. `AddHours` across Berlin's spring transition is resolved before the hour is read (`01:30 CET + 1h` → wall hour `03`), and changing the injected `Now` changes the nested result. The Date constructor has the same empty/formal propagation for matching component extractors; `Invalid(Date(...))` over an empty extractor source is OMISSION, not the VALUE polarity of a present unreal zero.

For `DateTime`, the date operand is any admitted date value (field / German date literal / `Date(...)` / the `ValueAsDate` placement) and the time operand any admitted time value (field / time literal / `Time(...)` / `TimeFromDateTime`). `TimeFromDateTime` requires a complete DateTime source, preserves a valueless source's reason, and projects only its **model-zone Hour/Minute/Second wall clock**; its internal 1970 carrier date and the source's original date/offset occurrence do not escape. In `DateTime(ValueAsDate(partial, LastDay), TimeFromDateTime(source))`, Date is evaluated first, then the projected clock is composed onto that resolved date; a formally unavailable Date side short-circuits before the Time arm. This also unlocks **direct DATE_TIME comparison**: `[ScheduledAt] == DateTime(OrderDate, PickupTime)` is kernel-valid, so a date-time field compares (`==`/`!=` and ordering) to another date-time value — a field, a `DateTime(...)`, or an `AddHours`-style shift. (Still rejected: a date-time field vs a *bare string literal* — `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`; build the value with `DateTime(...)`.)

**A computed Time retains that clock identity through storage and application (measured 2026-07-30, SPEC-2026-07-29-02).** `Time(Hour, Minute, Second)` and `TimeFromDateTime(2024-06-01T10:30:45)` both compute exact `10:30:45` under UTC and Europe/Berlin. The applied typed `DocumentV2` exposes the clock through a 1970-01-01 model-zone `Instant` (`1970-01-01T09:30:45Z` in Berlin), but a rule run after application matches `10:30:45` and does not match the carrier's UTC-decoded `09:30:45`; that `Instant` is transport, not Time identity. An impossible or missing hour and a formally invalid component clear a stale target. The five-channel result has one separate quirk: even a source target already containing `10:30:45` is classified in `getComputedFieldInstancesWithChanges` and is therefore applied to a different destination. Dynamic Groovy and generated Java agree on every arm; the exact cause of that same-clock classification remains deliberately unstated because source inspection alone does not discriminate it. *(Locked: `ComputedTimeTargetDiffTest` dual-kernel + interpreter matrix and multiplatform `ComputedTimeTargetTest`; interpreter finding IF238.)*

Modeled as arity-preserving `TimeConstruction.components` / `DateTimeConstruction` (Calculation) + a `DateTimeOperand` sealed interface (`DateTimeRef`/`DateTimeExpr`, orderable like dates/times) folded under `TemporalOperand`. Authored through the closed `TemporalComponent` union and the zero-to-three-argument `Dsl.time(...)` overloads, plus `Dsl.dateTime(date, time)`. *(Locked: `TemporalExtractorComponentLawsTest` for the exact placement/source gates; `TemporalExtractorComponentDiffTest` across dynamic Groovy, generated Java, and the interpreter; multiplatform `TemporalExtractorComponentTest`; the constant/arity owners `DateComponentConstantLawsTest`, `DateComponentConstantDiffTest`, and `DateComponentConstantTest`; `DateTimeExprReadTest`; `DateConditionTest`; BA-corpus `TimeConstruct`/`DateTimeConstruct`; N7 catalog examples. Reconciles SPEC-2026-07-27-12/-09/-07 and SPEC-2026-07-27-05.)*

**Point-in-time constants `Now` and `BaseYear` (implemented 2026-06-07; `Now` comparison domain corrected 2026-08-02).** The kernel's `PointInTimeOperationName` has three members — `Today` (a date, long modeled), `Now` (DE `Jetzt`), and `BaseYear` (DE `Referenzjahr`) — all carried as `IPointInTimeOperation`. `Now` is the current **date-time**; temporal ordering admits both date and date-time operands, while equality requires another date-time. `BaseYear` is the model's configured base year and is **polymorphic by typed context** (verified): an explicitly date-typed source uses the base-year start, while a number comparison, arithmetic expression, or Number computation uses the fixed scale-0 year. `BaseYear` is only valid in a model that declares a base year — `MVK_NO_BASE_YEAR` otherwise — so **modelkit gained `baseYear(int)`** (emits `modelInfo.baseYear` as a string; the kernel default is 2000). Modeled as `Now`/`BaseYear` (Calculation); the converter handles `Now` as a date-time operand and a date-ordering operand, and `BaseYear` as a date, date-time, and number operand. Authored via `Dsl.now()` (→ `DateTimeExpr`), `Dsl.baseYear()` (→ `DateExpr`), `Dsl.baseYearNumber()` (→ `NumberExpr`). *(Locked: `adapter.DateTimeExprReadTest.roundTripsNowAndBaseYear`, `NowDateOrderingDiffTest`, `NowMillisecondIdentityDiffTest`, `BaseYearArithmeticDiffTest`, and N7 catalog examples. The order fixture declares a base year.)*

**Sub-day time arithmetic over date-times (implemented 2026-06-07, family 2).** The kernel's `Add*`/`DifferenceIn*` families each carry three sub-day members alongside the date ones: `AddHours`/`AddMinutes`/`AddSeconds` (DE `Addiere{Stunden,Minuten,Sekunden}`) and `DifferenceInHours`/`DifferenceInMinutes`/`DifferenceInSeconds` (DE `DifferenzIn{Stunden,Minuten,Sekunden}`). They operate on **DATE_TIME** operands: `Add*` shifts a date-time and **returns a date-time** (it can roll the calendar day over — distinct from the date-returning `AddDays`/`AddMonths`/`AddYears`) while preserving an exact millisecond remainder supplied by `Now`; `DifferenceIn*` returns the signed epoch-millisecond delta divided by the unit in milliseconds, truncated toward zero. The shifted date-time composes as an extraction source — `HoursFromTime(AddHours(ScheduledAt, 2))` is kernel-valid. Modeled by widening `DateShift.Unit`/`DateDifference.Unit` with the three sub-day members (the shift unit carries its result kind, DATE vs DATE_TIME); the converter routes a DATE_TIME field through a `temporalOperand` helper (a `DateTimeRef` is a `TemporalOperand`, so it renders bare in argument position) and `convertTemporalSource` now accepts a shift as the extraction source. Authored via `Dsl.addHours`/`differenceInHours`/… over a `TemporalOperand` (the date `Add*`/`DifferenceIn*` factories widened from `DateOperand` to `TemporalOperand` too). *(Locked: `adapter.DateTimeExprReadTest.roundTripsSubDayTimeArithmetic`, `adapter.laws.DateTimeArithmeticDiffTest`, `NowMillisecondIdentityDiffTest`, `dsl.operators.DateConditionTest.rendersSubDayTimeArithmeticBilingually`, and N7 catalog examples.)*

## §6 supplement — min/max over DATE, TIME, and DATETIME ride a dedicated `DateCombiner`: NULL-date empty identity, valueless-operand skip, symmetric omission (source + differential, 2026-07-07; TIME/DATETIME added 2026-07-22 / SPEC-2026-07-21-07) <a id="kf95"></a>

> Fold: folded → §2 + §12.

(The NULL-date empty identity is canonical in §2 "aggregate identities"; the symmetric date polarity in §12's directional machinery; the combiner-dispatch mechanism stays as evidence.) The kernel dispatches `Min`/`Max`/`MinValue`/`MaxValue` **statically by operand type onto two combiner families** — numbers → `NumberCombiner` (`min`/`minWert`), **date-like (DATE, TIME, DATETIME)** → **`DateCombiner`** (`minDatum`/`minWertDatum`; the only non-number family — min/max over strings is not authorable) — and the two differ in three observable ways:

**All three date-like kinds ride the SAME `DateCombiner`** (`CheckFeldListenOperOpImpl`/`CheckFeldListenOpImpl` admit homogeneous DATETIME-base operands and mutually comparable component formats). The common fold selects by **resolved temporal order, never a rendered label**: **TIME** by its decoded **time-of-day** coordinate (time-only operands share one implicit model-zone anchor and have no standalone instant), **DATETIME** by its **resolved physical instant**. So a seconds-level TIME separation and two **equal-looking** `Europe/Berlin` fall-back-overlap DATETIME labels (`02:30` daylight vs. standard, 60 min apart) remain distinct candidates. The three observable behaviors below (NULL empty identity, valueless-operand skip, symmetric omission) hold identically for TIME and DATETIME.

The **typed surface** covers both temporal extremum shapes. For the entity-list `MaxValue`/`MinValue`, author with `Dsl.latestOf`/`earliestOf` (→ `DateExpr`), `Dsl.latestTimeOf`/`earliestTimeOf` (→ `TimeExpr`) and `Dsl.latestDateTimeOf`/`earliestDateTimeOf` (→ `DateTimeExpr`), all wrapping the shared `DateListAggregate` and all taking an operand LIST — a repetition list, a starred group, or two or more direct fields (DG38; the single-operand shape they used to take made the multi-field form both unauthorable and unreadable, [KF193](#kf193)); the adapter read boundary lowers the kernel extremum to the matching operand (`ConditionConverter.temporalExtremumKind`/`temporalListAggregate`), round-tripping through the DSL (locked by `adapter.TimeDateTimeAggregateReadTest`). For operand-list `Min`/`Max`, the overloaded `Dsl.min`/`max` preserve the homogeneous DATE/TIME/DATETIME family, while `ConditionConverter` recovers the exact kind hidden behind the kernel transport's common `OperationType.DATE` and converts the list on either side of a comparison (locked by `TemporalOperandMinMaxConditionTest` + `adapter.TemporalOperandMinMaxReadTest`; DG18 / API finding 92).

- **Empty identity.** The number combiner seeds `0` (§1 supplement — `MaxValue()` over all-empty == 0). The date combiner seeds `VkDate.NULL_DATE` — *no value* — and `BedingungsOperatorHelper.vergleicheDATUM` returns **false when either side's date is null**, so a comparison against an all-empty (or zero-row) date aggregate **never fires** (`FALSE_OR_UNKNOWN`), and a computation of it **clears** the target.
- **Operand-list emptiness.** `minDatum(d1, d2)`'s `VkDate.combine` **keeps the date-bearing side** when the other operand is valueless — an empty date operand is SKIPPED (`Min([OrderDate], [DeliveryDate])` with `OrderDate` empty is `DeliveryDate`), unlike the number form where an empty operand arrives as the substituted `0` and COUNTS. A malformed / required-empty date operand is nicht-prüfungsrelevant → the whole aggregate is suppressed.
- **Symmetric polarity.** `DateCombiner` tracks no directional `kannGroesserWerden`/`kannKleinerWerden` — only the symmetric **`nichtAngegeben`** (ORed over the operands' emptiness, plus `getValue(containsFilter)` marks any filtered result, plus the omitted-tail flag). A fired date comparison types **`TRUE_AF` (OMISSION) iff either side is nichtAngegeben — regardless of the comparison direction** (`RuntimeController.vergleicheDATUM`), where the number star's polarity is directional (§1/§3 supplement).

Comparison **typing** stays static and nominal: a quoted literal beside a date-valued min/max is a DATE literal (`"20.03.2026"`), and no date/text-vs-number comparison is authorable at all (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` / `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`) — so a runtime date-vs-number pair can only ever be evaluator-made, never input-legal. *(Interpreter: kind-aware fold identity + `minMaxOperandVals` + the `starFill` date branch + `producesDate` over the min/max family; the operand-list temporal fold keys a pure TIME by its decoded time-of-day and any dated value by its instant, IF204; locked by `adapter.laws.DateAggregateDiffTest` incl. a codegen tri-check — IF58 — and `adapter.laws.TemporalExtremaDiffTest` for the TIME/DATETIME extension incl. the Berlin overlap.)*

## §6 supplement — direct temporal comparison (coarse) vs temporal-extremum admission (exact) are TWO gates (source + kernel-route laws, 2026-07-22 / SPEC-2026-07-22-01) <a id="kf96"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

The admission format check for a temporal comparison and for a temporal **extremum operand** are deliberately different strengths — conflating them either rejects legal direct comparisons or admits incomparable extremum operands.

- **Direct comparison — coarse** (`CheckVergleichsBedingungImpl.checkDateType` → `DateFormat.formatsConsistentRegardingFormat(fmt1, fmt2, hasBaseYear())`). After optional Base-Year supplementation it requires only **matching YEAR presence** and **matching date/no-date class**; `==`/`!=` additionally require **matching time/no-time class**. It does **not** require identical component sets. Consequences (all kernel-locked): a `yyyy-MM` fragment `==` a `yyyy-MM-dd` date is **accepted**; a plain date `<` a date-time is **accepted** but `==` a date-time is **rejected** (`MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` — time-presence differs); a date `==` a time is **rejected** (date/no-date class differs); a year-less `MM` fragment vs a year-bearing date is **rejected without** a Base Year but **accepted with** one (the model year supplements the fragment).
- **Temporal extremum operand — exact** (`DateFormat.hasSameComponents` via `CheckEntityListenUtils.checkOpTypesAreComparableDatetimeType`). A multi-operand `Min`/`Max`/`MinValue`/`MaxValue` — and `NumberOfDifferentValues`, which shares the gate — requires **identical component sets**: the SAME `yyyy-MM` + `yyyy-MM-dd` pair that compares directly is **rejected** inside `Min(...)` with **`MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE`**; DATETIME extrema require all six components. It is component sets and **not format spellings** — the equal-set pairs `yyyy-MM-dd` + `dd.MM.yyyy` and `yyyy-MM` + `yyyyMM` are admitted — and **not declared kinds** either, since a DATE `yyyy` beside a DateFragment `yyyy` is admitted. A declared **Base Year** supplements `YEAR` into both sets first, so a yearless operand joins exactly when the rest already agrees ([KF193](#kf193)).

This is an authoring-admission distinction only; it does not touch resolved chronology or the extremum fold (that fold is the §6 min/max supplement + IF204). a12-dmkits **delegates both gates to the kernel** (the DSL's single-field extremum scope cannot express the multi-format operand list that trips the exact gate). *(Locked: `validate.laws.TemporalComparabilityGateLawsTest` — the coarse/exact separator, date-vs-date-time ordering-vs-equality, date-vs-time rejection, and Base-Year supplementation, all against the real kernel; neighbor `DateFragmentComparabilityLawsTest` owns the year-presence partition.)*

`CustomCondition <Name>` (DE `ApplikationsBedingung`; grammar `applikationsBedingung: 'ApplikationsBedingung' nameOhnePunkt`) is a bare predicate — a host-registered name, no operands. KERNEL-SEMANTICS §14 names two bans; both verified and now **pre-checked** (the constructs are representable):

## §2 supplement — the filled-count aggregates (2026-06-04 experiments) <a id="kf98"></a>

> Fold: folded → §2 + §9 + §12.

The behavioral half is canonical (§2's count-family override row; §12's grow-only counts; §3's invalid-operand non-evaluability); the authoring slot rules below stay here as evidence. `NumberOfFilledFields` / `NumberOfFilledGroups` (DE: `AnzahlAngegebenerFelder`/`AnzahlAngegebenerKontexte`; the grammar's `feldListenAnzahlOp` — its third sibling `NumberOfDifferentValues` is also implemented, see the list-aggregate slot laws below) are **numeric expressions**, freely comparable and usable in arithmetic (`NumberOfFilledFields(a, b) + 1 < [Q]` validates). Slot rules:

- **`NumberOfFilledFields` needs more than one field *or* at least one group *or* a single flattened repetition list** — a single plain field draws **`MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN`** ("There must be more than one field or at least one group"), but a single wildcard scope `Group*/field` is accepted (it counts filled reps). The group form counts the filled fields *inside* the group(s); multiple groups are legal. Field kinds may be **mixed** (boolean, enum, number together — it counts presence, not values).
- **`NumberOfFilledGroups` needs more than one group *or* a single repeatable group as a wildcard scope.** The same operand gate applies to rules and computations. Fixed pairs and triples of distinct, disjoint nonrepeatable groups are admitted, including a nested fixed terminal beside a disjoint sibling. A two-or-more group list may instead mix a starred repeatable group with fixed groups, as in `NumberOfFilledGroups(Items*, ShippingAddress)`, and a sole **repeatable** group written `Group*` is legal and counts that group's filled repetitions. The separators are exact: one fixed group draws **`MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDGN`**; an exact duplicate draws **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`**; ancestor/descendant overlap, including a root beside its contained group, draws **`MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`**; an unstarred repeatable group draws **`MVK_NO_WILDCARD`**; starring a non-repeatable group draws **`MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD`**; and a field argument draws **`MVK_NO_FIELDS_ALLOWED`**. These are static admission facts. In particular, accepting the starred computation forms does not establish their runtime behavior (reconciled from a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-09-01`, kernel-measured 2026-08-10).
- **Root groups: banned in `NumberOfFilledFields`** (**`MVK_ROOT_GROUP_REFERENCED`**, "It is not allowed to reference a rootgroup"), but **allowed in `NumberOfFilledGroups` as the sole, starred operand only when the root is repeatable**. `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Persons*)` over a repeatable root group validates; `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Order*)` over a non-repeatable root is `MVK_INVALID_WILDCARD` (source `checkNoRootGroupWhenMoreThanOneParameter`; probe-confirmed and corrected 2026-08-10).
- Comparing the count (derived scale 0) to a **decimal literal** with ordering (`<= 1.5`) is accepted because ordering bypasses the §5 equality scale gate; this is not evidence of a global literal exemption.

*(Locked: N7 examples of both operators including the param-size/type-direction invalids; `validate.laws.RootGroupCountLawsTest` covers the computation pair/triple, nested/disjoint, sole-starred, and starred/fixed admissions plus the four exact diagnostic separators, sole-starred-root acceptance, and non-repeatable-root wildcard refusal; the `NumberOfFilledFields` root-group ban is pre-checked in `CountAggregate` by `dsl.operators.AggregateConditionTest`. The typed API authors the kernel's distinct repeatable-root operation through `Dsl.numberOfFilledRootGroups` / `RootGroupCount`, while `CountAggregate` continues to own nested group lists.)*

**Runtime counting semantics (2026-06-10, RT-semantics drain — `anzahlAngegebenerEntities`):**

- **A formal-error operand makes the whole count non-evaluable** — the rule is suppressed; the broken field is neither counted as filled nor skipped (contrast `FirstFilledValue`, where a broken operand *after* the first filled one is invisible). *Discriminated 2026-08-24 by the three-rule design of [KF195](#kf195); the single-rule assertion this bullet first carried was satisfied by the skipping account too.*
- **The count can grow but never shrink**: with unfilled operands left, a fired comparison is an `OMISSION_ERROR`; with every operand filled, a `VALUE_ERROR` — a plain field list has no omitted-tail problem (unlike the starred aggregates, §9 supplement).

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.FilledCountLawsTest`.)*

**Generalizes to every NUMERIC COMBINER (2026-06-23, fuzz-found):** a malformed element makes the **whole combiner non-evaluable → rule suppressed**, not just counts. Probed: `Sum(Lines* / Price) > 100` with one `"abc"` element fires **only** `zahlHatUngueltigeZeichen`, never the rule. Holds for the starred aggregates (`Sum`/`MaxValue`/`MinValue`/`NumberOfDifferentValues`) and the operand-list `Min`/`Max` alike — a formal-error operand is "unknown", and an aggregate over an unknown is unknown. (Empties are different: the star drops absent/empty cells, so an empty row is *skipped*, not a suppressor; only a FILLED-but-malformed value suppresses.) **"Malformed" means FORMALLY invalid, not merely unparseable** — a fuzz seed caught that `-0` (a signed zero) *parses* as `0` yet is a formal error, so `Sum` over a `-0` element must suppress (the kernel does); the interpreter therefore decides aggregate-element validity by the **formal check**, not by parseability.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.AggMalformedDiffTest`.)*

**Corrected 2026-08-06 (cold review) — the scan IS ordered, but neither "it never surveys" nor "the gate it consumes" survives the source.** `combineFeldListe` walks the selection in authored order and early-returns `c.getNonRelevantValue()` at the first cell failing `isPruefungsRelevant` (runtime class `RuntimeController`). Three claims in this paragraph's first version were wrong, each confirmed against that source: (a) **not "never a survey"** — immediately *before* the loop, `if (sparsenessOptimization)` calls `istEineWiederholungNichtPruefungsRelevant(...)` under `validierungArt.isValidationPartWith3ValueLogic()` and returns non-relevant **without reading a cell**, which is the whole-repetition survey that leaves an all-rows aggregate UNKNOWN in partial validation even when every concrete row is enumerated (§12; locked by `PartialValidationAggregateDiffTest.concreteBothRowsOnlyFirstFilled`, already green and contradicted by the retracted wording). (b) **What separates `FirstFilledValue` is `Combiner.canChange()`, not the gate** — both operators pass the *same* `isPruefungsRelevant` call, and the loop's `if (!c.canChange()) return c.getValue(...)` lets `FirstValueCombiner`'s override (`value == null && !nonRelevantFieldBeforeFirstGiven`) leave a later cell's gate unevaluated; `FirstFilledValue` also passes `sparsenessOptimization = false`. A rule of the form "behavior follows from the relevance gate the operator consumes" predicts the SAME answer for `Sum` and `FirstFilledValue`, so it is **withdrawn**. (c) **Compute is a different mechanism, not this scan with a different outcome** — `CalculationCache.convertInvalidFieldsForCalculation` says so in the kernel's own words, converting invalid entities "so that nothing is treated as irrelevant, but causes exceptions to be thrown instead", with `resetErroneousEntitiesForValidation()` carrying `// don't treat any entity as "not relevant"`; the abort is the `valueProvider.apply(id)` read one line *after* the gate, via `getWertXML` -> `createCascadingError`.

**What is measured here is narrower than the retracted wording claimed.** For `Sum`/`MaxValue`/`MinValue`/`NumberOfDifferentValues`, the malformed cell's authored position does not change the **VERDICT** — head and tail both report `zahlHatUngueltigeZeichen` alone with the rule suppressed — while the formal error's pointer **names the offending row** (`[1, 1, 1]` vs `[1, 2, 1]`), so validation *output* is not position-blind and the earlier "cannot be read off validation output" was false. Scope: only `Combiner`-based operators reach `combineFeldListe`; `NumberOfFilledFields`, `NumberOfFilledGroups`, `NumberOfValueInFields` and `SumOfProducts` run their own loops with no `Combiner`, and `FieldValuesNotUnique` has **no early return at all** (a non-relevant cell is skipped; the return is at the first duplicate, [KF175](#kf175)) — which is precisely why it is a bad sibling to generalize from, the substance a12-kernel-lean asked for in SPEC-2026-08-06-01. The `CustomCondition`-in-`Having` refusal cited earlier is `MVK_DISALLOWED_CONSTRUCT_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` only when the filter carries another term; a filter consisting *only* of the custom leaf reports `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` first (`validate.laws.AggregateSlotLawsTest`). *(Locked: `adapter.laws.AggMalformedDiffTest.theMalformedCellsPositionDoesNotChangeAnAllRowsAggregateVerdict`, whose row column pins that the head/tail swap was applied. The ordered early return itself remains a SOURCE-level reading with no runtime witness — verdict identity is what BOTH an ordered stop and a survey predict.)*

**Both kernel strategies agree, and `SumOfProducts` is measured rather than inherited (2026-08-06).** The positional verdict is now tri-checked: dynamic-Groovy, the static-Java codegen strategy and the interpreter report the same thing for a malformed head, a malformed tail and an all-valid control. `SumOfProducts` is included deliberately, because it reaches **neither** `combineFeldListe` **nor** the three-value pre-survey, so nothing about its third-state behaviour may be inherited from the `Combiner`-based aggregates — and twice now it has been wrong where it was folded into a list with them (the partial-relevance correction at §12, and the withdrawn ordering rule above). Measured: a malformed cell in **either** zipped list suppresses it, and the position does not change that verdict, so an ordering claim of the "the FIRST reached formal failure is reported" shape has **no witness in validation output** for this operator either — the formal pass emits every invalid cell regardless, and the rule is suppressed either way. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.AggMalformedDiffTest.theStaticJavaStrategyAgreesOnThePositionalVerdictIncludingSumOfProducts`.)*

## §9 supplement — `RepetitionNotUnique`: per-row cross-row composite-key uniqueness (probe, 2026-06-24) <a id="kf101"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

The author-written **cross-ROW** uniqueness rule (vs `FieldValuesNotUnique`'s value-list, and the auto `uniqueIndex`). The rule sits at the **PARENT** group and iterates the keys' repeatable group; the error field is **inside** the repeated group, so it emits **one message per offending row**. Probed semantics:

- **Fires per row whose (composite) key DUPLICATES another row's** within the parent-row scope — `Count [5,5]` flags both rows (2 messages); `[5,7,5]` flags rows 1 & 3, not 2; `[5,7]` and a single row → none. A **composite** key is the tuple: `(Count,Weight) [(5,1),(5,2)]` distinct → none, `[(5,1),(5,1)]` → both flagged.
- **An ALL-empty key row is skipped** (`empty,empty` → none; `5,empty` → the empty row drops, the lone `5` is not a duplicate). But **among participants** (≥1 key field filled) **empties match empties**: a composite `(5,empty),(5,empty)` → the two rows ARE duplicates → flagged.
- **Polarity is directional**: an all-filled duplicate is **VALUE** (change a value); a duplicate whose key has an **empty (fillable) component** is **OMISSION** (`(5,empty),(5,empty)` → OMISSION — filling the empty `Weight` could make them distinct).
- **Keys are plain fields on one path** — no groups (`MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`), no asterisks (`MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`), all on a single path (`MVK_NOT_IN_SAME_PATH`); each must be repeatable relative to the rule group, so the rule must be authored at the PARENT (error field inside the repeated group), not inside it (`MVK_REPEATABLE_GROUP_MISSING`).
- **Key admission is by VALUE-VALIDATION, not field KIND; every non-Number key compares by exact STORED TEXT** (source + differential, 2026-07-22, SPEC-2026-07-22-10). `CheckWiederholungBedingungImpl` applies field/category/wildcard/semantic-index/value-validation gates but **no field-kind gate** (`CheckEntityUtils.checkIsValueValidation` rejects only the no-value-validation profile), so a direct **Enumeration, Date, Time, DateTime, Boolean, or Confirm** key is admitted alongside Number/String; a String configured without value validation is rejected (`MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`) as are groups (`MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`)/wildcards (`MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`)/semantic indices (`MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED`), and a category is not a referenceable operand. At runtime `RuntimeController.getWerteOrNullIfEinFeldNichtPruefungsRelevant` special-cases **Number as `VkBigDecimal`** (scale-19 value equality) and passes **every other kind through exact `feldWertIntern` STORED-text equality** — its nearby Number/String-only Javadoc is STALE. So a direct **Enumeration** key compares stored **tokens** (not the display label or category projection: two different tokens sharing one category do not duplicate), and a **Date/Time/DateTime** key compares stored text, never a parsed instant (fixed-width formats are 1:1, so there is no same-instant/different-text firing witness — only Number keys exhibit value-vs-spelling). The peer `RepetitionNotUniqueEvaluator` is already mechanism-aligned (Number → `rnuNumericKey`, every other declared kind → `KeyAtom.Exact`). *(Locked own-domain: authoring `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyKindLawsTest`; differential `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyKindDiffTest` (groovy-dynamic vs static-Java vs interpreter); multiplatform `interpreter … RepetitionNotUniqueKeyKindTest`.)*
- **It is a per-row 3VL PREDICATE; a guard conjunct gates firing, NOT the cache** (probe + source, 2026-07-07). `RepetitionNotUnique(key)` composes like any predicate: `<guard> And RepetitionNotUnique(key)` fires a duplicate row only when the guard also holds there, and the combined polarity follows the ordinary `And` (OMISSION if either operand is OMISSION; a formally-invalid guard operand → UNKNOWN → suppresses). Crucially the **duplicate cache is built over the full scope INDEPENDENT of the guard** — so a duplicate whose guard is FALSE does not fire, yet it still makes its partner a duplicate. Source, BOTH strategies: runtime `RuntimeController.wiederholungNichtEindeutig` builds the cache once (`RepetitionNotUniqueErrorCache.isInitialised`) over ALL rows in `ermittleWiederholungenMitDuplikaten`, then per-row returns `TRUE_WF`/`TRUE_AF`/`FALSE_OR_UNKNOWN`; codegen `EntityListCondition.st` emits a call to that same runtime method with a per-rule cache (so codegen carries no separate RNU semantics — runtime-parity ⟹ codegen-parity). *(Locked own-domain: `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueGuardedDiffTest`, incl. a groovy-dynamic vs static-JAVA tri-check.)*
- **A FORMALLY-INVALID key cell is EXCLUDED from the duplicate cache — per-KEY-CELL, not row-wide** (source + differential, 2026-07-07). The cache is built from **check-relevant** cells only: `ermittleWiederholungenMitDuplikaten` calls `getWerteOrNullIfEinFeldNichtPruefungsRelevant`, which returns null — the whole row is `continue`-skipped — the moment ANY key cell's `isWertAngegeben` is **UNKNOWN** (`= !isPruefungsRelevant =` the cell is marked `fehlerhaft`): a bad FORMAT, a duplicate-INDEX (`uniqueIndex`) cell, an over-repetition cell, **and a required-EMPTY cell**. **The required-empty case is a CORRECTION (2026-07-07, composite-key differential): a required-empty key cell IS UNKNOWN, not a valid participant.** The kernel's mandatory check is a **PRELIMINARY autogen rule** (`CodeGenRuleDefinition.isPreliminary()` = *"exactly the auto generated rules are preliminary"* → `MainValidatorController.preliminaryError(…, PFLICHT_FELD_FEHLER, …)` → `ValidationCache.markFieldAsInvalidForValidation`) that runs BEFORE the RNU rule builds its cache, so a required-empty cell is already `fehlerhaft` ⟹ `isWertAngegeben == UNKNOWN` ⟹ the row is dropped. Only an **OPTIONAL-empty** cell (a non-required field left empty) is `isWertAngegeben == FALSE` → a valid empty participant contributing a null key component. So the distinguishing property is **requiredness, not emptiness** (differentially: `(Sku,Count)` with `Sku` required+empty on both rows and `Count` duplicated fires **nothing**; the same shape with an OPTIONAL empty component fires OMISSION). Consequences: `RepetitionNotUnique(indexField)` over a duplicated index does **not** fire (each index cell is `uniqueIndex`-invalid → excluded → no two rows are "duplicates" in the check-relevant cache; only the auto `uniqueIndex` fires), and a malformed / required-empty key cell is likewise never a duplicate. The exclusion consults only the KEY fields (`entityList`), so a formal error on a NON-key field of the same row does NOT drop it — `RepetitionNotUnique(Count)` still fires on rows whose INDEX field is a duplicate. This is the exact sibling of the field-local `uniqueIndex` suppression above (§4 supplement, IF15). *(Locked own-domain: `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueFormalKeyDiffTest` — dup-index key, malformed key, composite required-empty key, fully-duplicated control, mixed rows, the clean-non-key control, + a groovy-dynamic vs static-JAVA tri-check; the OPTIONAL-empty participant by `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueDiffTest.compositeEmptyComponentIsOmission`.)*
- **Scope (the BA "basic version", no `@From`):** the **reference group** is the **first repeatable group BELOW the rule group** on the key path, and uniqueness is checked per that group's **PARENT row** — NOT per the key's immediate parent. So a key two repeatable levels deep (`/Project/Milestones/Tasks/Effort`, rule at `/Project`) is checked across **ALL** tasks of **all** milestones (scope = the `/Project` row), not per milestone (kernel-probed on the nested project fixture). For a single-level key (`/Order/Items/Count`) the two coincide. The **`@From _Group_`** selector (the `FromScope` path-op) **overrides the reference group**, scoping uniqueness per the named group's PARENT — so `@From Milestones` (reference Milestones) checks across all milestones (global), while `@From Milestones/Tasks` (reference Tasks) narrows to per-milestone (both kernel-probed on the project fixture). `@From` resolves relative to the rule group: a relative name/path, the `RuleGroup` keyword (the rule group itself — requires it be repeatable, else `MVK …must be repeatable`), `..` segments, or an absolute `/…` path. Naming the rule group by its own name (`@From Project`) is `MVK_INVALID_ENTITY` — use `RuleGroup`. The keyword is localized (`@From` EN, `@Von` DE), unlike the `In`/`IN` separators. **`@From` also counts as a REFERENCE for the error-field rule (measured 2026-07-25):** with `@From Tiers` the kernel accepts a rule whose error field is a `Tiers` field that is neither a key nor named anywhere else, while the same shape *without* `@From` draws `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` — so the keys' own group is **not** an implicit reference, but an explicit scope is. *(Locked: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyKindLawsTest` — both halves; rulekit's advisory heuristic `ConditionReferences` had omitted the scope and warned falsely on the legal shape.)*

**The boundary of that contribution — it is the whole SUBTREE, and two of the four candidate positions are closed by the WILDCARD laws rather than by the reference rule** (measured as a class 2026-07-25; answers a12-kernel-lean SG13). On a fixture whose *derived* reference group is the same group `@From` names — so the clause changes nothing but its own presence:

| error field position, relative to the `@From` group | with `@From` | without |
|---|---|---|
| **in** the group, not a key | **admitted** | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` |
| in a **descendant** of the group | **admitted** | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` |
| in the group's **parent** | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |
| in the **terminal key group** when it differs from `@From`, for the measured single terminal key plus distinct non-key error fixture | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_AND_ITERATION_INVALID` | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` |

So `@From` behaves like an enclosing **group** reference — everything under the group is covered, exactly as `covers()` treats a `GroupPresenceCondition` — and the *authored clause* is what does it: both admitting rows flip to a rejection when the clause is dropped even though the resolved scope is identical. **A consumer storing only the resolved reference group therefore cannot reproduce this rule and must retain an authored-`@From` marker.**

The two rejecting rows never reach the reference rule at all, and both are closed from *both* sides by the wildcard laws: an error field that does not pin a repeatable level makes the key reference demand a star there (`MVK_NO_WILDCARD` — "Missing specification of an asterisk for …"), while a star in an RNU key is refused outright (`MVK_NO_WILDCARDS_ALLOWED`). The resulting refusal is measured only for a **single terminal key with a distinct non-key terminal error field**. It does not generalize to a same-path composite containing an ancestor key and a descendant key that is also the error field: that shape is admitted with or without an ancestor `@From`, in either authored key order. *(Locked refusal boundary: `validate.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueReferenceBoundaryLawsTest`; locked admitted counterexample: `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueKeyOrderDiffTest`, dynamic Groovy + generated Java + interpreter.)*

*(Interpreter: `PredicateOp.REPETITION_NOT_UNIQUE` is an ordinary 3VL leaf in the normal boolean walk (IF149), not a top-level recognizer. `RepetitionNotUniqueEvaluator` builds the call-scoped duplicate cache once over the full scope, and `evalPred`/`predType` consume its per-row result wherever the leaf is composed; branch guards therefore affect combination/firing but never membership in the duplicate relation. The cache drops a row when any key cell is formally invalid, including `MANDATORY_FIELD`. Locked: `adapter.laws.RepetitionNotUniqueCompositionDiffTest` for nested/And/Or composition and `testRule`, plus `RepetitionNotUniqueDiffTest`, `RepetitionNotUniqueNestedDiffTest`, `RepetitionNotUniqueGuardedDiffTest`, and `RepetitionNotUniqueFormalKeyDiffTest` for scope, polarity, optional-empty participation, and invalid-key exclusion.)*

## §9 supplement — `SemanticIndex` (`[field For "value"]`): keyed row lookup, absent → empty value (probe, 2026-06-24) <a id="kf102"></a>

> Fold: folded → §10.

`[Field For "value"]` is the value of `Field` in the repetition whose **index field** equals `"value"` (the kernel's "semantic index" — by the index field, not the positional row number). Probed:

- A matched, **filled** cell yields its value — `[Items/Count For "SKU-1"]` is the `Count` of the Items row with `Sku == "SKU-1"`; `== 5` / `> 0` fire as VALUE.
- **No matching row OR a matched-but-empty cell both read as the kind's EMPTY value when the index column is clean** (a number → 0) — `[Items/Count For "SKU-1"] == 0` **fires (OMISSION)** when there is no `SKU-1` row or its `Count` is empty (the absent value is fillable); `> 0` / `== 5` do not fire. A clean missing key is not UNKNOWN. An unavailable, empty, or duplicated index cell compromises an otherwise unmatched lookup to UNKNOWN, including an empty field-valued query; that separate state is pinned in the presence supplement below.

*(Interpreter: `Expr.SemanticIndex(path, indexValue)` (parsed in the `[...]` atom via a `For "…"` clause); `EvalContext.indexedCell` resolves the canonical key through the memoized per-scope row inventory and shared admission/collision policy, returning the selected cell or null (→ the kind's empty value). The group's index field is resolved from the threaded `indexFields`; the polarity rides the standard `fill` (fillable iff the cell is absent/empty). Locked: `adapter.laws.SemanticIndexDiffTest` — matched value, other key, and the empty/missing OMISSION cases.)*

## §9 supplement — `SemanticIndex` PRESENCE: clean absence is FALSE, compromised absence is UNKNOWN (source + differential, 2026-07-07; amended 2026-08-09) <a id="kf103"></a>

> Fold: folded → §10.

An indexed ref is also a legal **presence operand** — `FieldFilled(Count For "SKU-1")`, `FieldNotFilled(…)`, or an operand of a fill quantifier (`AllFieldsFilled(Count For "K", Other)`) — and `FieldValueAsString(field For key)` reads through it. The kernel compiles `FieldFilled`/`FieldNotFilled` as one-operand `AllFieldsFilled`/`NoFieldFilled`; the indexed ref resolves a unique admitted key to at most one cell (`ValidationCache.resolveSemanticIndex` → `IndexFieldCache.lookup`; duplicates are unavailable) whose presence is the ordinary `isWertAngegeben` 3-state:

- a matched, check-relevant **filled** cell → TRUE;
- a matched row with an **empty** cell, an **ABSENT row** (no row carries the key), or an **empty/no-match KEY field** (the field-keyed `[X For KeyField]` form) over a **clean index column** → FALSE — an absent row is judged like an empty cell, **not skipped**, so `FieldNotFilled([X For "k"])` FIRES when no row carries the key;
- a **malformed** matched cell, a formally **invalid key field**, or an empty/no-match key over a column compromised by an unavailable, empty, or duplicated index cell → UNKNOWN (not check-relevant — neither the positive nor the negative presence fires).

`FieldValueAsString` over an indexed cell reads the matched cell's stored value; a matched-empty cell or clean no-match reads as `""` (which the `vergleicheSTRING` empty rule then suppresses in a comparison), while an unavailable query or compromised index column is UNKNOWN. *(Interpreter: `semanticIndexPresence` behind the shared `presenceTri`; locked by `adapter.laws.SemanticIndexPresenceDiffTest` — IF59.)*

## §9 supplement — `Having`: a per-row filter on a starred aggregate (probe, 2026-06-24) <a id="kf104"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

`Sum(Items* / Count Having <cond>)` (and the other aggregates) consume **only the rows for which the complete `<cond>` is known TRUE** — the filter is evaluated per repetition row before the aggregate. FALSE or UNKNOWN drops a candidate before the selected cell is consumed. Probed: rows (UnitWeight, Count) `(1,3),(2,10),(1,4)` with `Having [Items/UnitWeight] == 1` → the aggregate sees only the W==1 rows → `Sum == 7` (the unfiltered Sum is 17); `> 5` fires, `> 7` does not; `Having [...] == 9` (no matching rows) → `Sum == 0` fires. Polarity is the aggregate's own (Sum over a growable repetition → OMISSION). The filter is a full three-valued condition over the row's fields: ordinary composition still applies, so a complete `TRUE Or UNKNOWN` is TRUE and keeps the candidate.

Correlation does not exclude the current row implicitly: a same-group filter includes the current outer coordinate unless it carries an explicit `CurrentRepetition(G) != CurrentRepetition($G)`. That comparison is by the coordinate of the **named repetition level**, not physical-row identity; in an `A*/B*` candidate set, comparing `B` excludes every candidate with the outer row's `B` leaf index across different `A` rows. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.ValueListQuantifierHavingDiffTest` + `CorrelationLawsTest` + `SelfCorrelatedOverlapQuantifierDiffTest` + `MultiStarOuterCorrelationDiffTest`.)*

*(Interpreter: `Expr.Star` gained an optional `having: Cond?` (parsed from a `Having` clause on the starred operand in `readArgs`); `Interpreter.starVals` evaluates the filter in each per-row context (`EvalContext.rowContexts` → the Document's scoped `RowContext`s) and keeps the matching rows' filled values. Locked: `adapter.laws.HavingDiffTest`.)*

## §9/§11 supplement — the computation-phase filtered iterator PREFETCHES ONE KEPT SUCCESSOR before the current target is consumed (source + differential, both strategies, 2026-07-23; SPEC-2026-07-23-10/-11) <a id="kf105"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9 + §11.

Filter and target reads of a filtered field list are **interleaved by one kept-candidate lookahead**, not phased. `EbenenIterator.InnerIterator` initializes by searching forward for the first kept candidate (evaluating each complete candidate's `FilterPredicate.isRelevant`, skipping FALSE ones), and each `next()` advances to the NEXT kept candidate *before* returning the current one; `RuntimeController.combineFeldListe`'s consumer loop applies the value provider only to the returned identifier. During computation, `CalculationCache.convertInvalidFieldsForCalculation` makes any read of a formally-invalid cell throw, so the read ORDER decides which cell aborts the computation:

- a filter poison met while searching for a kept candidate's successor **precedes the pending current target** — a filled current `FirstFilledValue` target still CLEARS when the immediate-successor filter, or a filter reached through FALSE candidates, is invalid;
- once one successor is kept, the current target is consumed next — `FirstFilledValue`'s prefix stop (`FirstValueCombiner.canChange`) then leaves every filter **beyond that successor** unread, so a filled first target still WINS over an invalid third filter;
- an earlier terminal authored operand still hides a later filtered operand completely (the later slot's iterator is never constructed);
- the consume-every-row value aggregates (`Sum`/`MinValue`/`MaxValue`/`NumberOfDifferentValues`) ride the **same** iterator but drain it, so for them the lookahead changes only *which* poison aborts first — and that cause is **not observable**: the kernel's generated catch discards `CalculationFieldException.getInternalId()` and marks the target "fehlerhaft berechnet" silently (the interpreter's `PoisonedReadException` is equally cause-blind at its `ComputationEngine` catch). Eager whole-selection filtering and the kernel's lookahead are therefore outcome-EQUIVALENT for the draining aggregates; the read-order boundary is outcome-observable exactly through the prefix consumer `FirstFilledValue`. Validation is untouched — its filter reads are 3VL row-drops (never aborts), so the kept-row stream is order-insensitive there.

*(Interpreter: one shared lazy `keptRowsWithSuccessorLookahead` sequence in `ExprEval` now serves both consumers — `firstFilledScan` keeps the prefix stop, `starOperandVals` keeps the full fold; locked `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueKeptSuccessorDiffTest` (red→green on the successor-filter poison) + `adapter.laws.AggregateKeptSuccessorDiffTest` (the aggregate agreement locks) + multiplatform `FirstFilledValueKeptSuccessorTest`/`AggregateKeptSuccessorTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF214.)*

## §9 supplement — the star-binding anchor: the `*`-marked level ALWAYS iterates fully; only levels STRICTLY ABOVE the star bind to the enclosing row (differential, both strategies, 2026-07-09) <a id="kf106"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

A starred operand read from an ITERATING row (a per-row rule, or a per-row computation's operand/precondition) enumerates its rows by binding the enclosing iteration's indices only for the repeatable levels **strictly above the starred group** — the `*`-marked level itself (and anything below) always iterates its **full** range. So a bare **same-group star** (`MaxValue(../Pricing* / Helper) == [Helper]` in a per-row rule ON Pricing — the BA "predecessors" shape without the filter) spans **ALL rows**, not the current one: only the max row(s) fire. An **ancestor star** read from a deeper row (`MaxValue(../../Pricing* / Helper)` per Tier row) spans all Pricing rows, not the row's own ancestor. A star **nested below** the iterating row (`Sum(Items* / Amount)` per Order row) still binds the Order row — the standard cross-level case, unchanged. This is coherent with the `$` design (KERNEL-SEMANTICS §9): `$` inside a `Having` is the ONLY outer-row correlation — a bare star never correlates. Differentially pinned in BOTH modes and BOTH strategies (groovy-dynamic == java-static): validation per-row fire sets AND per-row computation preconditions agree. Compute-side corollary (the IG44 R2 atom): the all-rows span makes a per-row dependent's aggregate READ a poisoned sibling cell — one poisoned cell aborts every row's dependent ("fehlerhaft berechnet"), where an own-row collapse would hide it. *(Interpreter: `Document.RowContext.starRows` caps the shared prefix at the starred group's parent — the same anchor `rowContexts` always used; locked `adapter.laws.ComputeStarAggregatePoisonDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter … SameGroupStarBindingTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF93.)*

**…and a CROSS-SUBTREE star binds only along the SHARED named ancestry — never positionally (differential, both strategies, 2026-07-10).** A starred group in a **different subtree** read from an iterating row — `NumberOfFilledGroups(/Root/Settings/Regions*)` in a per-`Claims`-row rule (the kernel team's own "an error text per supported language" metamodel shape: `NumberOfFilledGroups(ErrorMessages*) < NumberOfFilledGroups(/MVK/ModelProperties/SupportedLanguages*)` per `Rules` row) — binds the enclosing row's indices only for the ancestor levels the two named chains **share** (here: the root); from the subtree fork down, the starred chain iterates fully. So the cross-subtree count/presence is **identical from every iterating row**: the rule fires per row on ALL rows (kernel-pinned via `NumberOfFilledGroups`, `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`, and the reversed-polarity `NoGroupFilled`, groovy-dynamic == java-static). An enclosing row's index is never applied **positionally** to an unrelated chain. (A stored condition may carry embedded newlines/indentation inside an operator's parens — the MVK metamodel does — lexed as hidden-channel whitespace.) *(Interpreter: `Document.RowContext.groupScopePrefix` — the group-star row scope (`rowContexts`/`correlationBuckets`) now applies the same `commonPrefixLen` guard `starRows` (IF93) always had; locked `adapter.laws.CrossSubtreeGroupStarDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter … CrossSubtreeGroupStarBindingTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF97.)*

**…and a bare GROUP reference is an iteration anchor of its own — ancestor-or-SELF, per row, judging the row's cells; the ERROR ENTITY is not an anchor (differential + kernel-captured corpus cases, both strategies, 2026-07-10).** A group-scope quantifier argument may reference a repeatable group WITHOUT a star only when the rule's error field sits INSIDE it (otherwise `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` — "missing specification of an asterisk"): the rule then iterates PER ROW of that group and the quantifier judges the CURRENT row's cells

**Corrected 2026-08-15 — the index-keying conjunct was a fixture confound and is withdrawn.** This entry read "only when the group is INDEX-keyed (`indexFieldName`) **and** the rule's error field sits INSIDE it" until a12-kernel-lean challenged the claim's fixture. The original fixture varied index-keying and error-field locus together, so the two conjuncts were never separated. The separating control is one builder call: the SAME model with and without `indexField("Sku")` on the repeatable group produces a **byte-identical** 24-cell accept/reject matrix (4 field-fill quantifiers × starred/bare × three error-field loci), so **index-keying is not a gate here at all — the locus alone admits the unstarred operand.** Our own `GroupListDiagnosticIdentityLawsTest` had corroborated this from the other side the whole time: its `Parcels` is repeatable with no index field and still shows locus selection. The withdrawn half had propagated into KERNEL-SEMANTICS §9 (corrected) and into a peer spec via our handback (§17 of the outbound letter, amended). *(Locked: `validate.laws.UnstarredRepeatableGroupIterationLawsTest`.)*

**…and the SECOND gate, once the operand is admitted, reads neither polarity nor truth (measured 2026-08-15).** `MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` invites the reading "negative quantifiers are refused inside an iteration". Both directions refute it: `FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled(Items)` is grammatically negative and is **admitted**, while `NumberOfFilledFields(Items) < 1` contains no negation and is **refused**. Nor is the gate semantic — on a count that cannot go below zero, `< 1`, `<= 0` and `== 0` are the same predicate, yet `< 1` is **refused** where `<= 0` and `== 0` are **admitted** (`< 2`, `<= 1`, `!= 1` refused; `>= 0`, `> 0`, `>= 1` admitted). So the analysis is **syntactic**, it is the kernel's (`IterationNotValidVisitor`), and a consumer must not reimplement it from either the operator name or the condition's truth set. The kernel's own message states the intent — *"the rule can fire for not filled repetitions of this repetition level"* — but the implementation does not decide it by evaluating that. *(Locked: same class.)*

**…and composing the two gates on a NESTED repeatable: the unstarred levels must be a PREFIX of the authored chain (measured 2026-08-15).** The wildcard gate (authored slot, per level) and the iteration gate (error-field locus) had each only been measured on a **single-level** repeatable, where "the operand's own level" and "the level the error field makes iterable" are the same level and cannot disagree. Over a nested `Sections`(rep) ▸ `Answers`(rep) fixture, 24 cells (4 spellings × 2 polarities × 3 error-field loci) give one law: **an unstarred level may not sit below a starred one.** `Sections*` then a bare `Answers` draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` in **all six** of its cells — no polarity and no error-field placement rescues it, so **a star does not cover the levels beneath it**. The other three spellings follow from the prefix rule: fully bare iterates both levels and needs the error field inside the inner group; bare-then-starred iterates only the outer, so the error field may sit anywhere inside it (`Title` or deeper in `Answers`), and both refuse an error field outside; fully starred has no unstarred level, hence no iteration, hence no locus requirement and no polarity gate — admitted in all six. The polarity refusal tracks the **iterated** level exactly: bare-then-starred takes `NotAllFieldsFilled` happily with the error field in `Title` (the starred inner set is folded, not iterated) and draws `MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` with the error field inside `Answers`. Neither gate alone predicts the starred-above-bare row, which is the one a second implementation composing them separately will admit. *(Locked: `validate.laws.NestedGroupOperandGateLawsTest`.)*

**A `Having` filter cannot ride a GROUP operand at all on the field-fill carrier (measured 2026-08-15).** `AllFieldsFilled(Sections* Having …)` and every sibling — both spellings, both polarities, both error-field loci — draw **`MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED`**, while the identical operand *without* its filter is admitted exactly where the gates above say it should be. The unfiltered controls are what attribute the refusal to the filter rather than to the group. So the filtered form belongs to a **field** operand (`Sum(Lines* / Amount Having …)`) and the two gates have no filtered domain to compose over here — "does a filter move the wildcard or iteration gate" is not merely unmeasured on this carrier but unaskable. *(Locked: same class.)*

**Extended 2026-08-15 — the refusal is CARRIER-WIDE, now measured on three unrelated carriers.** The same `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` fires for a `Having` on a group operand of the **uniqueness** carrier (`FieldValuesNotUnique`) and the **first-filled** carrier (`FirstFilledValue`), each paired with its unfiltered control (admitted) and with the FIELD form of the identical filter (admitted) — so the refusal is charged to the filter riding a group, not to the group operand, which these carriers accept, nor to the model being unable to carry a filter. With the value aggregates already measured the same way (§ "a VALUE AGGREGATE accepts a GROUP operand"), the general statement is that **a filter belongs to a field operand on every carrier measured, and no carrier admits one on a group operand.** The practical consequence is that any "does a reached filter change X for the group form" question is **unaskable** rather than open — which is how the last of a12-kernel-lean's three group-operand residuals closed, after four rounds of being reported as unmeasured when authoring it took one test. *(Locked: `validate.laws.GroupOperandFilterLawsTest.aHavingFilterCannotAttachToAGroupOperand`.)*

**Extended 2026-08-31 — POSITION and the COMPUTATION arm, and the refusal is STATIC, not only at code generation (measured, a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-08-31-09`).** Every row above sits on a **single-operand** carrier and on the **validation** arm, so two thirds of that entry's claim was untested here rather than confirmed. On the group **count** — the carrier the entry names, and the only measured one whose operands are all group paths — `NumberOfFilledGroups(Counts* Having …, Recounts*)` and `NumberOfFilledGroups(Counts*, Recounts* Having …)` both draw `MVK_NO_GROUPS_ALLOWED` while the unfiltered pair is admitted, so the filter site is refused wherever it sits. The same three rows on a **computation**'s operation give the same three verdicts, which is a measurement rather than a corollary: the two arms elaborate a starred group operand through different code — the compute path expands it and carries the filter onto each expanded field, while validation's group-aware arm is gated on the filter's absence (`adapter.laws.FilteredGroupStarFillDiffTest`) — so their agreement is two gates concurring, not one gate seen twice. Each positional row's filter reads its own group's field, since a filter naming a different group's field is a separate question with a refusal of its own; varying both would have made the row uninterpretable. The diagnostic names the site, *"At 'Having': It is not allowed to use a group."*, and does **not** echo the condition, so the code is attributable without re-parsing the rule. And there is no operator-level spelling to fall back to: a filter written **after** the operand list, `NumberOfFilledGroups(Counts*, Recounts*) Having …`, is a parse error, `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN` — so with the six carriers now measured, no spelling attaches a filter to a group operand anywhere.

**…and the LAYER axis, which no entry asked for and which our own two earliest locks had left implicit.** `FilteredGroupStarFillDiffTest` (fill quantifiers) and `GroupStarValueAggregateDiffTest.havingOnGroupStarIsRejectedByTheKernel` (`Sum`) both reach the refusal as a **throw at code generation**, and a reader of either would conclude that is where it lives — the first even says so. Measured on both those carriers, **static arbitration refuses it as an ordinary diagnostic**, which is the only answer a consumer authoring against `checkConsistency` ever sees; the throw is how those two paths meet the refusal, not the layer that owns it. Both files' claims were corrected in the same pass. *(Locked: same class — `theGROUPCOUNTRefusesAFilterAtEitherOperandPosition`, `theCOMPUTATIONArmRefusesTheSameShapeAtEitherPosition`, `theDiagnosticNamesTheFilterAsTheSite`, `theSTATICArbitrationRefusesItOnTheCarriersOnlyMeasuredAtCodegenBefore`.)*

The original per-row reading stands unchanged — `FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled(OrderInformation)` (a real-workspace idiom) fires exactly on the rows that are individually PARTIALLY filled, at each row's own pointer; every-row-complete, all-empty-row, and no-rows instances are silent (groovy-dynamic == java-static). The DECLARED repetition range plays no part. The error entity itself does NOT drive iteration — a rule whose error field sits deeper-repeatable than its condition refs keeps the refs' scope (pinned by the kernel-captured conformance cases). *(Interpreter: `scopeFromRefs` treats a GROUP ref ancestor-or-self; the per-row group fillScope was already row-correct once the scope was; locked `adapter.laws.CollectivelyFilledGroupScopeDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter … GroupRefRuleScopeTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF106.)*

**…and a rule's iteration is REFERENCE-driven — a rule with NO repeatable non-starred ref evaluates ONCE, anchored at its error entity, regardless of its declaring container's content (differential, both strategies, 2026-07-10).** A real-workspace `*_Rules` container ROOT declares rules whose references and error entities all live in OTHER roots (e.g. "the membership end is covered by no contract" — a filtered `NumberOfFilledFields(…) == 0` over `/Contracts/Contract*`, erroring at `/Membership/LinkEnd`): the kernel fires it exactly once at the error entity even though the declaring container has NO instance content (groovy-dynamic == java-static). The declaring group matters for resolving relative refs, never for iteration or content-gating. *(Interpreter: `iterationContexts` re-anchors a no-repeatable-ref rule at its error entity's parent when the declaring scope yields no contexts — the ordinary-rule sibling of IF100's implicit-validation anchor; locked `adapter.laws.CrossRootRuleScopeDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter … CrossRootRuleScopeTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF103.)*

**Corrected 2026-08-09: compatible NESTED references select the DEEPEST path with per-parent outer resolution, but validation iteration is not limited to stored inner rows.** A condition reading an outer (`Lines/Weight`) and an inner (`Lines/Items/Qty`) derives the INNER scope with complete parent coordinates: `[../Weight]` resolves against the current row's OWN line, so a row exceeding another parent's limit but not its own stays silent. The original zero-child probe used a positive child guard; its silence could not distinguish no evaluation from an implicit empty child whose guard was false. The discriminating `Qty < 5` rule shows the real boundary: every existing repeatable parent with no concrete nested child contributes child row 1 to validation iteration, recursively, and that empty-as-zero comparison fires OMISSION there. An absent outermost repeatable group still contributes no row. The implicit context is not stored content: `GroupFilled(RuleGroup)`, mandatory/`uniqueIndex`, starred group/index operands, parallel identity, and computation continue to see stored V2 rows only; `RepetitionNotUnique` deliberately consumes the validation iteration rows. The operator-sensitive `MVK_NEG_CONDITION_IN_ITERATION` admission law remains unchanged, but it is not a blanket proof that no accepted condition can fire on an implicit row. *(Locked: `adapter.laws.RepeatableRowContentDiffTest` for the positive three-level discriminator and consumer split; `ReferenceDrivenIterationScopeDiffTest` for deepest-path/per-parent resolution and positive-guard controls; multiplatform `ReferenceDrivenIterationScopeTest` for the host projection. Interpreter treatment: [IF277](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if277).)*

**…and a MULTI-star operand binds at the FIRST `*`-marked level; `NumberOfFilledFields` honors a `Having` filter (differential, both strategies, 2026-07-09).** For `A* / B* / F` read from an iterating row, only the levels strictly above **A** (the first star) bind — a per-`B`-row read spans ALL of `A`'s rows (kernel-pinned for a filtered count AND an unfiltered `Sum`). And the count aggregate `NumberOfFilledFields(star Having <cond>)` consumes only filter-kept rows, exactly like the value aggregates (`anzahlAngegebenerFelder` rides the same filtered `EntityIterator`): the filter drops rows FIRST — a malformed cell in a dropped row does not suppress the count — and a KEPT row's malformed cell makes the count non-evaluable. A `$`-correlated filter (`[X] == [$X]`) resolves against the computing/iterating row, giving the "count my duplicates across the whole list" idiom real corpus models use. *(Interpreter: `Expr.Star.bindDepth` threaded through the star family; the count gained the filtered loop; locked `adapter.laws.MultiStarFilteredCountDiffTest` + multiplatform `interpreter … MultiStarFilteredCountTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF94.)*

**…and the same first-star boundary governs declared-tail polarity at every reopened level (tri-differential, both strategies, 2026-07-21).** For `A*/B*/C*/F`, the aggregate remains fillable/OMISSION-typed when any in-scope `A` capacity is missing, any actual `A` lacks a declared `B`, any actual `A/B` lacks a declared `C`, or an instantiated leaf cell is empty. An unbounded starred repetition always retains that open tail. A flattened `leafRowCount < C.repeatability` test is therefore wrong: it loses missing outer and middle branches. Repeatable levels strictly above the first `*` remain bound and their unused declared tail does not taint the aggregate. *(Interpreter: a cached per-scope hierarchical child-count proof, O(actual rows × star depth) with no Cartesian enumeration; locked by `MultiStarDeclaredTailPolarityDiffTest` + `StarOnlyIterationScopeDiffTest`; INTERPRETER-FINDINGS IF194.)*

## §9 supplement — a STAR-ONLY condition scopes at the star's BINDING levels; with no repeatable reference level the rule fires ONCE, root-content-gated, at the pinned first-row anchor (source + differential, both strategies, 2026-07-18) <a id="kf107"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.
> (2026-07-24, with the reference-driven rewrite: the headline scope law — star binding levels iterate, the starred level collapses — and the once-evaluation anchor are canonical; the 16-arm evidence, root-content gate, and phantom-anchor pinning stay here.)

The star-only completion of the reference-driven iteration law above: when a rule's condition carries **no per-row (non-starred) repeatable reference at all**, its iteration scope comes from the starred refs' **BINDING levels** — the unindexed repeatable levels **strictly above the first `*`-marked group** carry the per-row ITERATION marker exactly as a non-starred ref's ancestors do, while the starred level and everything below are a WILDCARD collapse and never iterate.
