**What the refusals do and do not license.** Each refusal makes a corresponding interpreter path unreachable *through the kernel's own validator* — the missing group branch in `minMaxOperandVals`, and the deliberately unexpanded group case in the `filteredStarCells` path `DateRangesOverlap` shares. It does **not** make them unreachable: `Expr` is public API, our parser accepts a bare group path as a function argument, and `dmtool rule eval --condition` evaluates an arbitrary condition with no MVK pre-flight at all (the native binary carries no kernel). So "the kernel refuses it" bounds what a *stored, validated* model can contain, and nothing more.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.GroupOperandCarrierAdmissionLawsTest` — one asserted table whose verdict rides in each row rather than in a lookup with a `default -> ACCEPT` arm, so a mistyped label can no longer silently downgrade a refusal expectation. The fixture carries a homogeneous group per field kind in both repetition shapes, since a mixed group's expansion offends the kind gate first and its rejection then cannot distinguish "this carrier refuses a group" from "this carrier refuses these kinds". Every ACCEPT family carries an explicit-field control; the `Min`/`Max` and `DateRangesOverlap` refusals carry an admitted field control each, and the starred-group cells additionally carry the starred-field row that separates the wildcard gate from the group gate.)*

## §9 supplement — the WILDCARD gate reads the AUTHORED slot, so a group operand covers nested repeatable levels that an explicit field path must star itself (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-15) <a id="kf188"></a>

> Fold: pending — it belongs beside the arity/category split in the §9 group-operand table, which [KF187](#kf187) has not folded either.

A group operand whose expansion crosses a **nested repeatable** group is admitted without the author naming any inner star: `FieldsNotCollectivelyFilled(Sections*, Note)` is ACCEPTED where `Sections` repeats and contains a repeatable `Answers`. The **same expansion written out** is refused: naming `Sections*/Answers/Text` draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` — *"Missing specification of an asterisk for 'Sections/Answers'"* — and starring both levels is accepted again, which is the control that attributes the refusal to the missing inner star rather than to the spelling.

So this is the **third** gate in the split [KF187](#kf187) opens, and it lands on the *authored* side with arity rather than on the *expansion* side with the kind/category gate:

| gate | reads |
|---|---|
| arity (`MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN`) | the **authored** slots — a group is already-many ([KF187](#kf187)) |
| **wildcard (`MVK_NO_WILDCARD`)** | the **authored** path — a group operand is checked at its own level only |
| kind / category (`MVK_VARYING_TYPES_NOT_ALLOWED`, `MVK_NO_NUMBER`, …) | the **expansion** ([KF187](#kf187), [KF173](#kf173)) |

**Why it is worth its own entry rather than an inference from either neighbour.** The two rows say opposite things about the same operand, so neither predicts this one: an implementation that reasoned "the kind gate reads the expansion, therefore every gate does" would expect the group form to be refused, and one that reasoned from arity alone would have no view on the explicit form at all. It also has a direct consumer consequence — **any rewrite of a group operand into its expansion must star every repeatable level it crosses**, because what the kernel waves through as a group it refuses as a path. Ours did, twice, until the rewrite itself was removed ([API-FINDINGS](API-FINDINGS.md) finding 124).

**The RUNTIME counterpart, and the reason it needs a two-field group to state (tri-engine compute differential, 2026-08-31, `OverLimitOperandComputeArmDiffTest`).** A group operand's extent is every field of the declared kind beneath it, not one distinguished field: over a repeatable `Items` holding `Amount` and `Surcharge`, `Sum(Payouts)` answers **15** where `Sum(Payouts/Items*/Amount)` answers **12** on the identical document (`Amount` 5 + `Surcharge` 3 in row 1, `Amount` 7 in row 2). This is measured rather than assumed because **a single-field group cannot separate it**: where the group owns one number field, "the operand names its group's whole subtree" and "the operand names the one field it has" agree on every document, and every earlier group-operand row in this repository sat on such a group. a12-kernel-lean hit the same blind spot on their own estate — every group in their fixtures owned exactly one field, and the over-general clause was one carrier away from shipping (their `LF114`). The fixture, not the row set, is where that confound hides, which is why the question to ask of a claim is what every model it was measured on has in common that a reader would not assume.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.GroupOperandCarrierAdmissionLawsTest` — three rows in the sweep's own table: the group operand over a nested repeatable ACCEPTs, its written-out expansion with the inner star missing draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, and the same expansion fully starred ACCEPTs as the control. The lock sits at the accept/reject tier rather than in the converter test that first surfaced it, because it is a kernel fact and outlived the consumer defect: DG36 removed the rewrite entirely, so no converter test can carry it any more.)*

## §9 supplement: `FirstFilledValue` completes exact duplicates in AUTHORED ORDER before checking strict overlap (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-17) <a id="kf189"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-17-01` confirmed its individual eight rows but refuted the mechanism inferred from its one all-fault row. The peer measured `(Fixed, Fixed/First, Fixed/First, Fixed)`: the repeated direct field completes before the repeated fixed group, so `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1` names `Fixed/First`. That row cannot distinguish a direct-field class priority from an authored-order scan.

The within-model discriminator reverses only which repeat completes first: `(Fixed, Fixed, Fixed/First, Fixed/First)` still emits exactly one `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`, but now names `Fixed`. Therefore the static sequence is:

1. Scan every non-wildcard entity slot in authored order and stop at the first exact identity seen twice, regardless of whether it is a field or group.
2. Only when there is no exact duplicate, reject a fixed group beside its strict descendant with `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`.

The full maintained matrix also confirms the surrounding branches: one fixed group is admitted; the same fixed group twice draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`; the same starred group twice is admitted as two authored slots; one direct field draws `MVK_PARAMSIZE_INVALIDN`; the same direct field twice draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM1`; fixed group plus descendant draws `MVK_DUPLICATE_PARAM2`; and a fixed-group duplicate pre-empts a simultaneous overlap. This is static admission evidence only. It establishes neither runtime expansion nor evaluation order.

*(Locked: `validate.laws.FirstFilledValueDuplicatePrecedenceLawsTest`, nine complete-code rows plus both exact witness paths through the real kernel; `dsl.operators.FirstFilledValueDuplicatePrecedenceTest` locks the typed owner's matching pre-check, wildcard preservation, strict-overlap fallback, and independent singleton arity.)*

## §9 supplement: fixed-group `FirstFilledValue` scans stable model declaration order with prefix polarity (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-18) <a id="kf190"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-17-02` at local revision `b5f8bb0ec5f9e75cd0066ae1253d7c869a609310` confirms the complete four-row matrix against the maintained runtime owner. The model deliberately declares paths in the opposite order from their lexical sort: `ZetaDirect` before `AlphaDirect`, then `ZetaNested/Value` before `AlphaNested/Value`. Dynamic Groovy, generated Java, and the interpreter all select `ZetaDirect` when both direct fields are filled and `ZetaNested/Value` when both nested fields are filled; the second-only controls select the corresponding `Alpha` declaration, proving the later declaration remains reachable.

The matrix also separates the value result from its message type. Selecting the first direct field is VALUE even though every later nested declaration is empty. Selecting the second direct field or either nested field is OMISSION because an earlier declaration was reached empty. The group therefore enters the ordinary directional prefix scan as a declaration-ordered cell stream; it is not pre-collapsed to one complete/incomplete group flag.

No evaluator change was required. The existing typed `BoundModel.firstFilledGroup` preserves the authored group owner, `Document.containedFields` supplies recursive model declaration order, and `Document.containedFieldCells` yields each declaration's instantiated cells to the existing `firstFilledScan`. No schema or probe route was added.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.FirstFilledValueGroupOperandDiffTest.aFixedGroupUsesStableDeclarationOrderAndPrefixPolarity`, exact selected token plus VALUE/OMISSION on both kernel strategies and the interpreter; `FirstFilledValueGroupOrderTest.fixedGroupUsesStableDeclarationOrderAndPrefixPolarity`, the same four rows on JVM and Node.)*

## §9 supplement: starred-group `FirstFilledValue` traverses declaration-major across rows (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-18) <a id="kf191"></a>

> Fold: folded → §9.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-17-03` at local revision `ac924d381b6a55fff74d6b26fb3de5802887893f` confirms its six-row matrix against the maintained runtime owner. With row 1 `Second = second` and row 2 `First = first`, dynamic Groovy and generated Java select `first` with OMISSION, so the traversal is declaration-major rather than row-major. The independent controls reach row 1 `Second` when no `First` is filled and row 2 `First` when row 1 `First` is empty. An immediate row 1 `First` is VALUE despite a later instantiated row, proving unread suffix rows and declared capacity do not taint a terminal value.

The two fallback controls agree with the existing no-row field-star family: both zero instantiated rows and one instantiated empty row before a filled direct fallback select the fallback with OMISSION. A no-row group star is therefore a not-given prefix, not a neutral empty stream.

No evaluator change was required. The existing typed `BoundModel.firstFilledGroup("/Return/Rows*")` retains the starred group operand, and `firstFilledExpandedGroup` consumes `Document.containedFields` in declaration order before `firstFilledStar` scans each field's rows. This is the same interpreter scan and differential route as the fixed-group owner; no schema, second evaluator, or probe route was added.

## The consistency gate's diagnostic list is NOT a defect count, in either direction (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-22) <a id="kf192"></a>

> Fold: not-foldable — this is a property of the consistency GATE's output, not of any kernel-semantics section; its consumer-facing home is the `diagnostics` contract of `schema result`.

Two independently live defects can return **one** diagnostic, and **one** defect can return **two**. Both were measured on the same fixture and the same condition text, varying only the error field, so the pair is a within-model control on a single variable.

| error field | condition | codes returned |
|---|---|---|
| `../MonthOnly` (referenced) | `AllFieldsFilled(MonthOnly, YearOnly) And [MonthOnly] == [YearOnly]` | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` |
| `../Ref` (exists, unreferenced) | *a comparison the kernel accepts* | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_REFERENCED` |
| `../Ref` (exists, unreferenced) | **the same year-class mix** | `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` **only** — the error-field objection is suppressed |
| `../Nope` (does not exist) | **the same year-class mix** | `MVK_ERROR_FIELD_MISSING` **and** `MVK_MISSING_ERROR_FIELD` — two codes for one defect, and now the *comparison* is suppressed |

The first two rows are the controls: each code fires alone, so in row 3 the missing one is suppressed rather than absent. Row 4 is what makes the finding two-sided, and it also **settles the layer question without appealing to our own source**: two kernel codes travel the whole path intact, so row 3's single code cannot be dmtool dropping one.

Note the precedence **reverses** between rows 3 and 4 — the comparison wins over an unreferenced error field, and a missing error field wins over the comparison. A plausible mechanism is that a missing error field is a model-shape objection raised before the rule-semantics checks while an unreferenced one is raised after the comparison check, but that is a HYPOTHESIS from these two observations and is not measured.

**Consequence for a consumer** (the reason G55 was filed): read a lone diagnostic as *an* objection, never *the* objection. To attribute a refusal to a specific gate, remove the other candidate defect and re-run — which is exactly what the reporting campaign had to do. An author never notices, because fixing defects one at a time re-runs the gate anyway.

**Denominator, stated:** two multi-defect pairs on one fixture. Enough to establish that suppression and code-duplication both occur, which is what stops a consumer counting; not a general law about which gate wins, and no wider sweep was run.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.DiagnosticMultiplicityLawsTest` — both controls plus both multi-defect rows. Published in the `diagnostics` contract of `schema result`.)*

## §6/§9 supplement: the temporal AGGREGATE gate reads component SETS (Base-Year-supplemented); only `FieldValuesNotUnique` reads the format STRING (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-24) <a id="kf193"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-23-16`, **accepted**. Their entry corrects a clause of *theirs* that had said the aggregate gate reads the declared format "exactly as `FieldValuesNotUnique`'s does". This repository already held the two gates apart and correctly — [KF96](#kf96) names `DateFormat.hasSameComponents` for the extremum and [KF173](#kf173) the identical declared **format string** for `FieldValuesNotUnique` — so nothing here was wrong. Three things were nevertheless missing, and each is now measured and locked.

**1. The separating pair was never locked.** Every previously locked row is satisfied by *both* readings: a same-format pair is admitted under either, and the `yyyy-MM` + `yyyy-MM-dd` pair [KF96](#kf96) rejects differs in its component set *and* its spelling. Only an **equal-set, different-spelling** pair discriminates. Two exist, and both behave the same way on both carriers, in one model:

| operand pair | component set | `MaxValue` / `MinValue` / `NumberOfDifferentValues` | `FieldValuesNotUnique` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `yyyy-MM-dd` + `dd.MM.yyyy` | {Y, M, D} — equal | **ACCEPT** | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_DATE_ALLOWED` |
| `yyyy-MM` + `yyyyMM` | {Y, M} — equal | **ACCEPT** | `MVK_ONLY_STRING_ENUM_NUMBER_DATE_ALLOWED` |
| `yyyy-MM-dd` + `yyyy-MM` | differs | `MVK_DATEFORMATS_NOT_COMPATIBLE` | (refused, same class) |
| `yyyy-MM-dd` + `yyyy-MM-dd` | equal, same spelling | ACCEPT | ACCEPT |

Two gates, two codes, and neither is derivable from the other: `CheckEntityListenUtils.checkOpTypesAreComparableDatetimeType` → `DateFormat.hasSameComponents`, versus `OperationResultType` → `DateFormat.hasSameKnownFormatStringIfExists`.

**2. A declared Base Year supplements the YEAR component *inside* the aggregate gate.** `hasSameComponents(other, hasBaseYear)` adds `YEAR` to **both** sets before comparing, so a yearless operand joins exactly when the remaining components already agree — `MM` with `yyyy-MM`, `MM-dd` with a complete date — while both stay refused against the year-only `yyyy`, and a genuine set difference among two year-bearing operands (`yyyy-MM-dd` beside `yyyy-MM`) is not lifted either. The same Base Year does **not** reach `FieldValuesNotUnique`, which localizes the supplementation to this gate rather than to a shared pre-pass.

**3. The gate reads the temporal FAMILY, not the declared kind — and that half was a live over-rejection here.** A DATE declared `yyyy` beside a **DateFragment** declared `yyyy` is **admitted** (two kinds, one component set), while a DATE beside a TIME or a DATETIME is refused: the gate separates date-presence and time-presence, then compares sets. `DateListAggregate` was pre-checking *kind equality*, which refuses the admitted cross-kind pair — a client-side refusal broader than its measured basis, corrected here to a temporal-class check.

**Carrier scope, measured rather than assumed.** All three aggregate carriers (`MaxValue`, `MinValue`, `NumberOfDifferentValues`) route to the same gate, at all three operand shapes: an explicit field list, a direct field beside a starred list, and a non-repeatable GROUP whose expansion is the differently-spelled pair. `Sum` never reaches it — a temporal operand is `MVK_NO_NUMBER` outright. `FirstFilledValue` routes through a different checker arm (`checkAllFieldsMatchingOperationType`) and is **not** covered by this entry.

**What the reconciliation cost, and why it was not documentation-only.** Locking the separating pair needed an explicit two-field temporal `MaxValue`, which the typed surface could not express: `DateListAggregate` held a *single* operand. The read path was the worse half — `ConditionConverter.temporalExtremumKind` bailed out on any entity list longer than one, so a kernel-legal `MaxValue(FiledOn, ClosedOn)` fell through to the numeric arm and `rule read` returned the rule **Opaque** with *"MaxValue takes number fields; /Claim/FiledOn is DATE"*. A legal model was unreadable, not merely unauthorable. Both halves are fixed under DG38 (API finding 127).

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalAggregateComponentSetLawsTest` — 22 rows against the real kernel: both equal-set pairs on both carriers with their same-format controls, the differing-set refusals, the four Base-Year rows including the two that stay refused and the `FieldValuesNotUnique` non-lift, the cross-kind DATE/DateFragment admission with its TIME and DATETIME class controls, the starred and group operand shapes, and the `Sum` boundary. `adapter.MultiOperandTemporalExtremumReadTest` locks the read half — the two-field DATE and TIME extrema and the direct-plus-starred mix round-trip through the DSL, beside the kernel row that says the shape is legal.)*

## §6 supplement: `DateFromDateTime` reads the source label's OWN wall date, and ONE complete-DateTime source gate serves BOTH extractors (tri-engine differential + kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-08-24) <a id="kf194"></a>

> Fold: folded → §6.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-23-13`, **accepted**; no interpreter defect. Three additions, each measured here rather than transferred from the `TimeFromDateTime` sibling whose account [KF94](#kf94) already carried.

**1. The reading is the label's own date, with the time dropped and no zone conversion — and the existing coverage could not have shown it.** `DateTimeExtractDiffTest` already read year, month, and day out of a `DateFromDateTime`, but at a **midday** label (`10:30:45`), where the wall date and the retained instant's UTC date are the same day at every ordinary offset. The rival account — resolve the instant, take *its* date — is the natural implementation and the one that is silently off by a day. Only a label within the zone offset of midnight separates them, and the new fixture **controls the zone** rather than observing it: with `Europe/Berlin` declared, a stored `2024-06-15T00:30:00` is `2024-06-14T22:30:00Z`, so the two accounts predict different days. Two rival rules are authored side by side; the wall rule fires alone, on dynamic Groovy, generated Java, and the interpreter alike. *(This is deliberately stronger than the upstream measurement, which had to record its `+0200` host zone as ambient and therefore kept a scope limit here; declaring the zone removes it.)* The midday row fires **both** rules — so the time really is dropped and the separator is not passing by accident — and a row whose candidates match neither reading fires nothing, so a silent row is informative.

**2. The result is a DATE, and the refusals are what establish that.** It compares against a Date field, against `Today`, and against another `DateFromDateTime`, and it is the Date operand of `AddDays` and of `DateTime(...)`. Admissions alone would not separate a Date result from a DateTime one that merely compares well; the four `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` refusals do — against `Now`, against a `TimeFromDateTime` result, against a TIME field, and against the very DATE_TIME field it was extracted from.

**3. One complete-DateTime source gate, shared.** A **plain DATE field** is refused `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` *at the operator* under `DateFromDateTime` **and** under `TimeFromDateTime`. [IF301](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if301)'s time-only-DateTime table already recorded that class for a source missing its *calendar*; that a source missing its *clock* draws it too means the gate asks "is this a complete DateTime", not "does the format retain a date".

**And the operand grammar is narrower than a general date expression:** the operand is a bare path, so `DateFromDateTime([Moment])` is `MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN`; the extraction is refused as a `Date(...)` **component** with its own `MVK_DATE_OR_TIME_EXTRACT_OP_NOT_ALLOWED`; and it is not a `DifferenceInDays` operand at all. That `Date(...)` row is the one that needed a control, and the control corrected the reading: a Number field in the same position draws a *different* code (`MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`), so the refusal is keyed on the extract-op rather than on "the component is not a literal". Nesting inside an ordinary component extractor (`DayFromDate(DateFromDateTime(…))`) stays admitted, so "narrower grammar" must not be read as "never nests".

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DateFromDateTimeWallDateDiffTest` — the Berlin near-midnight separator plus its midday, all-negative, and UTC-zone controls, tri-checked on both kernel strategies and the interpreter; `rulekit.validate.laws.DateFromDateTimeSurfaceLawsTest` — 18 static rows against the real kernel covering the five admissions, the four comparison refusals, the three source-gate rows, and the three grammar rows with their two controls.)*

## §2/§3 supplement: the filled count separates EMPTY from INVALID, and the one-rule assertion that claimed it could not (tri-engine differential, 2026-08-24) <a id="kf195"></a>

> Fold: folded → §2.

Reconciliation of a12-kernel-lean `SPEC-2026-08-23-14`, **accepted**; no interpreter defect and no prose correction. The behavior was already recorded here in [KF98](#kf98)'s runtime-counting bullet — a formal-error operand makes the whole count non-evaluable, neither counted nor skipped. What the peer's entry actually supplies is the **experimental design**, and that mattered: our lock asserted the claim with a single `count == 2` rule that does not fire on a filled-beside-invalid row, and **all three rival accounts satisfy that assertion**. A skipping implementation counts `1`; a counts-it-as-filled implementation counts `2` and fails only the claim, not the test. The claim was true and untested.

**One count, three rules, four rows** — each rival now predicts a different firing rule on the row that matters:

| row | a skipping impl fires | a counts-as-filled impl fires | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| filled + **invalid** (`2024-02-30`) | `COUNT_1` | `COUNT_2` | **nothing** |
| filled + empty | `COUNT_1` | `COUNT_1` | `COUNT_1` |
| filled + filled | `COUNT_2` | `COUNT_2` | `COUNT_2` |
| empty + empty | `COUNT_0` | `COUNT_0` | `COUNT_0` |

The three non-invalid rows are each other's controls, so the silent row is an informative negative rather than a fixture that never fires. Dynamic Groovy, generated Java, and the interpreter agree on every row.

**Emptiness and invalidity are two states in this operator, not one** — the all-empty row is the second delta rather than a control: it counts `0` and compares normally instead of answering unavailable. That is what stops a consumer collapsing "no value" into "unknown" here.

**The count needs no computation-arm rule of its own, and the reason is structural.** `NumberOfFilledGroups` needs one because an invalid *descendant* leaves its group operand present, so the operator must still decide what to count; a field count's invalid operand **is** the operand, so [§11](KERNEL-SEMANTICS.md#11-computations)'s general operand-poison rule fires first and the target is cleared with the invalid operand named. Recorded as the explanation for an asymmetry that otherwise reads as a special case.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.FilledCountInvalidOperandDiffTest` — the four rows above on both kernel strategies and the interpreter. The neighbouring `adapter.laws.FilledCountLawsTest` keeps the growable-count polarity rows it already owned.)*
