There is no A12-owned pointer STRING for this kind, which is *why* the probe needs a two-arm policy at all, and why a spelling read off that artifact can only ever report the branch. The vector is the portable fact.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.MessagePointerVectorDiffTest` — the scope pair, read off `repetitionIndexes()` rather than off any rendered form.)*

## §1 supplement — starred group threshold quantifiers read only in-capacity parent environments (kernel `validateFull` + `validatePart`, 2026-09-01) <a id="kf229"></a>

> Fold: folded → §1.

The earlier two routes appeared to require an impossible sparse positional document: instantiate over-limit `Lines[3]` without the automatically materialized `Lines[1]` and `Lines[2]`, then ask whether `NoGroupFilled(Lines*)` or `AtLeastOneGroupFilled(Lines*)` sees row 3. That separator is unnecessary. A repeatable parent is dense, but a nonrepeatable descendant can be present under exactly one parent row, so the parent prefix can remain fixed while the quantifier's only filled witness crosses the capacity boundary.

One capacity-2 model and one full-validation document carry two structurally symmetric child groups under `Lines*`:

| starred child operand | only filled witness | result |
|---|---:|---|
| `Lines*/InCapacityMarker` | `Lines[2]` | `AtLeastOneGroupFilled` fires |
| `Lines*/OverCapacityMarker` | `Lines[3]` | `NoGroupFilled` fires |

Both dynamic Groovy and generated Java return that pair. If the threshold quantifiers ranged over every instantiated parent, the second row would instead fire `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`; the dense predecessor rows cannot explain it because they contain no `OverCapacityMarker` witness. The two carriers differ only by the parent repetition holding their filled descendant.

Partial validation supplies an independent carrier on the original `Lines*` operand. With the same dense three-row document fixed, making only row 2 relevant fires `AtLeastOneGroupFilled`; making only over-limit row 3 relevant leaves both threshold rules silent. The error field remains relevant in both calls, and a no-group-row-relevant call is the non-vacuity control.

The result reconciles `SPEC-2026-08-31-17`: `NoGroupFilled(G*)` and `AtLeastOneGroupFilled(G*)` quantify over the instantiated **in-capacity** rows, while a created-but-empty row inside that extent is filled structurally. `NumberOfFilledGroups(G*)` already read the same capacity extent. The interpreter's shared `Document.overLimitRows` exclusion matched every new row, so no runtime change was needed.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.StarredGroupQuantifierCapacityDiffTest` — count ladder, full-validation descendant separator, partial row-relevance separator, both kernel code-generation strategies, and interpreter agreement.)*

## §9 supplement — the declared-capacity projection reaches the String, Boolean and Confirm value counts and survives the REFLEXIVE `Having`, which separately flips every filtered carrier to OMISSION (kernel `validateFull`, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf230"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends the over-repetition evaluation-domain account; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Answers five a12-kernel-lean entries on independently authored carriers: `SPEC-2026-09-01-03` (String), `SPEC-2026-09-01-04` (Boolean, both constants), `SPEC-2026-09-02-01` (Confirm), `SPEC-2026-09-02-02` (all three, filtered) and `SPEC-2026-09-02-04` (the filtered Number aggregates). Every predicted count reproduced on the first run of each file.

**Why these were not corollaries of the Number row we already held.** The starred-field row in [KF58](#kf58)'s over-repetition family measures `NumberOfValueInFields` on a scale-0 NUMBER carrier only, so reusing it on a String, Boolean or Confirm declaration would transfer a mechanism across the carrier boundary. The filtered form is a second boundary, and that one is measured rather than argued. Our unfiltered star excludes over-limit rows in `Document.starRows`; a mutant disabling that filter is killed by the plain-carrier file and **SURVIVES** the filtered one, so a `Having` operand never reaches it and the unfiltered locks cannot speak for the filtered form. The converse does not hold: a mutant on `Document.rowContextsScoped`, the filtered route's own site, is killed by **both** files. Why the plain file reaches that helper is not established here — the call graph offers `groupListEnvironments` as a candidate and this batch did not discriminate it — so the asymmetry is claimed one-directionally, on the direction whose survival was observed.

**Every kind excludes the over-limit row, in the plain form.** Capacity two, the sole match in row 3: `NumberOfValueInFields("SALVAGE" In Categories*/Label)`, `(True In Reviews*/Approved)`, `(False In Reviews*/Approved)` and `(True In Consents*/Waiver)` answer `0`, `0`, `2` and `0`; the same content one index lower answers `1` on all four. With both in-capacity rows matching and the OPPOSITE value above capacity, the second Boolean constant is discriminating in its own right and answers `0`.

**The reflexive filter changes nothing about the extent.** Under `CurrentRepetition(G) == CurrentRepetition(G)` — every row selected, no value read, so `filtered` is the only variable — a Number star answers `Sum 5 · MinValue 5 · MaxValue 5 · NumberOfDifferentValues 1` where in-capacity row 1 holds `5` and over-limit row 3 holds `7`, against `12 · 5 · 7 · 2` for a complete-row account. Reversing the two values makes the filtered value count discriminating and it answers `0`. The three token kinds answer `0` on the same documents and `1`/`2` on their in-capacity controls. **Only this filter is measured**, and only the carriers named: an Enumeration/category token star is not probed on either arm, and a12-kernel-lean's own `SPEC-2026-09-02-02` records the opposite result there, so nothing here transfers to it.

**…but the filter DOES change the polarity, on every carrier including the aggregates.** All eight filtered carriers type `OMISSION_ERROR` on all four documents, where the plain analogue types the same counts `VALUE_ERROR` on the corresponding ones. That extends the rule this project already held for the value count alone — a filtered operand is growable unconditionally *because a filter is present* ([`NumberOfValueInFieldsPolarityDiffTest`](../adapter/src/test/kotlin/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/adapter/laws/NumberOfValueInFieldsPolarityDiffTest.kt), IF114) — to `Sum`, both extrema and the distinct count, and shows it holding on the in-capacity controls rather than only where the projection excluded something. It also corroborates a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-02-02` separator, whose three filtered token counts they report as `OMISSION_ERROR`.

**The polarity is recorded, not predicted.** An in-capacity domain whose cells are all filled types the fired count rule `VALUE_ERROR`; the Confirm carrier, whose in-capacity cells are absent while the count can still grow, types it `OMISSION_ERROR` on the same document. Both engines and the interpreter agree on the type as well as the value.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.StarredFieldValueCountCarrierCapacityDiffTest` — four carriers × a four-member exact-count ladder over three documents; `adapter.laws.FilteredStarCapacityExtentDiffTest` — eight filtered carriers over four documents, with the rendered condition asserted to carry its `Having` so the file cannot silently duplicate the unfiltered locks. Both assert the over-repetition finding is lit exactly on the documents holding a row above capacity, and both are mutation-checked against their own exclusion site.)*

## §6/§11 supplement — a bare Date CONSTANT reaches the target's opt-in pre-1900 policy after rendering, and a DateTime constant is judged against TWO zones (kernel `checkConsistency` + `compute`, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf231"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends the constant-assignment account of [KF222](#kf222)/[KF223](#kf223); folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-01-01` and `SPEC-2026-09-01-02` on independently authored carriers, every predicted cell on the first run. `-01` supersedes their earlier universal "a Date constant has no target check at either time" claim, and this measurement is what our own estate had not covered: [KF222](#kf222) established that the target's declared FORMAT decides a constant's admission and its store, with omitted components dropped silently — but a target's *value* policy is a separate gate, and both of our pre-1900 locks drove the target from a document cell rather than from a constant.

**The policy applies to a constant, and the pair is what shows it.** Two ISO `yyyy-MM-dd` Date targets differing in exactly one builder call (`rejectBefore1900`) receive the identical `"31.12.1899"` constant from two computations of one model on one document, at every instantiated row: the guarded target is **ERRORED retaining `1899-12-31`** — rendered into its own declared format, never cleared — and the unguarded twin is a **VALUE**. `"01.01.1900"` into a third guarded target is a VALUE, so the guard is a threshold rather than a blanket refusal of constants.

**A DateTime constant is judged twice, against two DIFFERENT zones.** With the model bytes and their declared `Europe/Berlin` fixed, `31.03.2024T02:30:00` — a wall time Berlin skips, its 2024 transition moving 02:00 straight to 03:00 — is **admitted** by `checkConsistency` under a UTC JVM default and **refused** under a Berlin one. So the static gate reads `TimeZone.getDefault()`, not the declared zone. Under the admitting default the runtime refuses the label anyway: it yields **no computed outcome at all** — not a cleared one and not an errored one — and one `berechnungsWertFehler` `VALUE_ERROR` per instantiated target row in `formalErrorsInOperands`. That falsifies "the runtime reads the JVM default"; it does **not** discriminate the model's declared zone from any other zone that also has no instant for this label, because the separating case — a second model declaring a zone in which the same wall time is ordinary — was not built. a12-kernel-lean's own entry hedges the same way, and the shared claim is the pair of verdict DEPENDENCIES rather than the conversion mechanism. `05.03.2024T12:30:00` is the control: admitted under both JVM defaults, and it stores `2024-03-05T12:30:00` per row with an empty operand-error channel.

**Both reproductions exposed the same interpreter defect, and it is fixed** — a bare temporal literal was not typed by its assignment target, so the German text reached the store uncanonicalized and every constant was flagged errored ([IF318](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if318)). *Corrected 2026-09-05:* the residual classification split recorded here — the kernel reporting no outcome and an operand error where the interpreter reported an ERRORED target — is closed too, the interpreter now treating an unresolvable label as the no-value operand failure it is ([IF326](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if326)). The separating case this entry declines to claim (a second model declaring a zone in which the same wall time is ordinary) has since been built on the INTERPRETER side only, so it constrains our classification and still supplies no kernel row.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DateConstantTargetPolicyDiffTest` — the guarded/unguarded pair with its threshold control, on a repeatable level, tri-engine, with the retained attempt and its bucket asserted separately so a clear cannot pass; `adapter.laws.DateTimeConstantZoneSplitDiffTest` — the 2×2 static grid over label × JVM default, the runtime outcome/operand-error channels, the declared zone read out of the model bytes, and (since 2026-09-05) the unresolvable label's cross-estate parity on both channels, with the seeded-target arm supplying the unprojected outcome comparison.)*

## §8 supplement — the custom-field-type SPI's CODEC is opt-in per presentation and off the validation path, while a MISSING validator raises from the full check (kernel SOURCE + runtime, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf232"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends the custom-extensibility surface; folds into §8 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Answers a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-02-05` and `SPEC-2026-09-02-06`, both of which asked for an observation their project cannot reach because it does not host the factory.

**A registered custom field type is a triple, and their source read of its shape is confirmed** at kernel 30.8.1: `ICustomFieldValidator extends ICustomFieldType` (the predecessor with the per-declaration `configData` map, `@Deprecated(forRemoval)` since 30.6.0, removal tracked as `A12K-3589`), with `validate(value, valParam, isDisplayValue)` beside `convertDisplay2Internal`/`convertInternal2Display`. Acceptance's complete input list is confirmed from the OUTSIDE as well as from the source: an instrumented validator records `validate(value, min, max, errorMsgLocale, isDisplayValue=false)`, the bounds being the field's declared ones and the param object `CustomFieldTypeValidationParamImpl(errMsgLocale, minLaenge, maxLaenge)`.

**The conversion arm has exactly ONE engine-side caller, and it is opt-in.** Enumerated across the kernel checkout (`grep` for both method names over `--include=*.java`, excluding `/build/`, `delombok`, and the api/impl modules that *define* or *implement* them): `FormatDefinitionVordefiniert.convert` is the only Java-runtime invocation site, gated on `darstellungsInfo.doConvertCustomFieldType(name)` — the caller's own `PresentationInformation` (`CONVERT_CUSTOM_FIELD_TYPES_ALL` / `_LIST`) — with the direction chosen by `vonXml`: XML ingress calls `convertInternal2Display`, everything else `convertDisplay2Internal`. That same flag supplies the `isDisplayValue` argument to `validate`. Measured consequence, which is what the entry asked for: on the ordinary `validateFull` path **neither** conversion is invoked on **either** code-generation strategy, and `isDisplayValue` is `false`. The instrument records **both overloads** of each arm, which is load-bearing rather than thorough: the engine calls the two-argument forms, whose SPI default returns a no-conversion result without delegating to the one-argument form, so an instrument watching only the outer pair would have reported an empty log whatever the engine did. The first version of this measurement had exactly that hole and a cold review found it. So a consumer modelling acceptance alone is complete for that path; a custom-typed cell has two texts only for a caller that asked for them.

**A missing validator raises, and the raise is reached from the FULL check.** `getCustomFieldValidator` throws `ValidatorException("Custom field validator '<name>' missing.")` when the lookup finds nothing — and the two sources are ALTERNATIVES, not a fallback chain: a supplied factory is asked and the static `CustomFieldTypeService` registry is consulted **only when no factory was supplied at all**, so a static registration does not rescue a factory that answers empty. The measured branch below is the supplied-factory one; the no-factory branch is read from source and not exercised here — but `validiereFormat` returns `Valid` before touching the factory when `fullCheck` is false, so the qualifier is load-bearing. Measured end to end: the model **parse does not reject** the missing registration, a filled relevant cell then raises with the type's name in the chain, and an EMPTY cell reaches neither the validator nor the raise. This corrects our own earlier claim's shape, which had been travelling on a docstring as the bare "no validator → it THROWS".

**Extended 2026-09-04 with the separator that makes the whole-call loss measurable** (a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-04-06`, whose runtime half both estates had recorded as holding no retained observation on either side). The raise does not replace the offending field's finding with a formal message beside the others — it escapes the call, so the document receives **no validation result at all**. That is only visible against what a clean control PRODUCES, so the model now carries a second rule that does not read the custom cell: with the cell empty the unregistered factory answers exactly what the registered one does, `HOLDER_SET` included, and with the cell filled those same messages are lost with the call. A field-level rejection would have left them in place. Scope, corrected 2026-09-04 after the probe's fault capture landed: their side could only observe **one strategy**, because the abort ate the second before it ran. Ours is now measured on **both** — the same model shape through `:adapter:kernelProbe` raises at `validateFull` on groovy-dynamic *and* generated Java, with `enginesAgree: true`, so the strategies agree on the fault (`adapter.laws.KernelProbeFaultCaptureTest`). The message-loss rows above remain the dynamic-Groovy arm's. **Our own answer to their acceptance is a THIRD shape, neither of the two it offered** — the interpreter reports the cell on a separate `unsupported` channel with no formal error and validates the rest of the document normally, a deliberate divergence recorded with its reason in [IF26](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if26).

**Their distrust of a source-shaped raise prediction was well placed, and the two extension points do differ.** The neighbouring PREDEFINED-type SPI degrades instead — an unregistered name fires both `Valid`/`Invalid` polarities as ordinary `VALUE_ERROR` messages with nothing raised (`adapter.laws.PredefinedTypeValidityDiffTest`), which is what refuted `EXP-2026-08-04-01`. Same-looking question, different SPI, opposite answer; neither result transfers to the other.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.CustomFieldTypeSpiInvocationLawsTest` — an instrumented validator whose every arm appends to one ordered log, so "no conversion was invoked" is the content of a list that demonstrably received the acceptance entry; both strategies; the missing-registration raise, its message, and the empty-cell control.)*

## §1 supplement — a non-deciding `GroupNotFilled` leaf is invisible even on the POLARITY channel, so its three-valued state is a free choice (kernel `validateFull`, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf233"></a>

> Fold: pending — a reachability result about the scalar group-presence leaf; folds into §1 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Answers a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-02-03`, which moved their scalar `GroupNotFilled` leaf from unknown to false for a relevant group carrying **both admitted content and an independent formal error**, and asked either for alignment or for a leaf-observable witness. There is none to give, and that is the result rather than an absence of effort.

**Why the rule-firing channel cannot decide it, and why one more channel was worth trying.** A12's condition language has no negation combinator, so a leaf occurs only positively and Kleene `And`/`Or` are monotone in the truth order — a leaf moving from false to unknown can never turn a silent rule into a firing one, which is the point their entry already makes. What that argument does **not** cover is the omission-versus-value TYPE of a rule that fires for another reason, and the typing walk is a separate computation over the same tree. So the probe fires every rule from a second disjunct — `Or(GroupNotFilled(G), FieldNotFilled(Anchor))` with `Anchor` empty — and reads the type.

**Two controls on two axes, and both are needed.** Across groups: `Clean` (content, no error → the leaf is false under both accounts), `ContentFreeError` (rejected content only → unknown under both), and `Mixed` (content **and** an independent error → the disputed cell). Across families: the same three leaves fired once from an omission-typed disjunct and once from a VALUE-typed one. Measured on both code-generation strategies and the interpreter: the type varies with the OTHER disjunct — `OMISSION_ERROR` for the whole first family, `VALUE_ERROR` for the whole second — and never with the leaf. The second family is what makes this a reading rather than a fixture property: without it every row fired from one predicate and a uniform polarity would have been constant by construction, which is the confound a cold review caught here on 2026-09-03.

**Disposition, corrected 2026-09-03: the last candidate channel is CLOSED, and the estates now agree by decision.** Stated at its measured width, this entry establishes that **the polarity of a rule fired by another disjunct does not see the leaf**, on both disjunct polarities. It left one candidate unprobed — a `Having` predicate carrying the leaf, where an unknown filter could make an aggregate unavailable while a false one merely excludes a row. That premise is now refuted: a filter conjunct that is not true drops its own row and leaves the aggregate available at its ordinary value ([KF234](#kf234)), so the filter position collapses false and unknown exactly as firing and message typing already do. No channel either estate has named can arbitrate.

On that footing the owner accepted a12-kernel-lean's alignment offer (2026-09-03) and this project's scalar `GroupNotFilled` now answers FALSE for a relevant group holding admitted content beside an independent error, where it answered UNKNOWN before. It is a COHERENCE decision, not a correctness one: the leaf is the Kleene complement of the presence product the GROUP-fill quantifiers already read, so one presence notion now serves both instead of two. `GroupFilled` is unchanged and a content-free erroneous group remains unknown. Because no kernel oracle can see the change, the lock is a projection unit test ([`GroupPresenceLeafProjectionTest`](../interpreter/src/commonTest/kotlin/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/interpreter/GroupPresenceLeafProjectionTest.kt)) over the complete `filled × erroneous × relevance` space, and the type-equality lock below stays exactly as it is so a kernel upgrade that made polarity leaf-sensitive reopens the question here.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.GroupNotFilledErroneousLeafDiffTest` — the three-way type equality asserted rather than described, so a kernel upgrade that made the polarity leaf-sensitive fails here; plus a fixture control proving the formal findings really land on exactly the mixed and content-free groups.)*

## §9 supplement — a non-true `Having` conjunct drops its OWN ROW and leaves the aggregate available, and the empty-as-zero rule does not reach a malformed operand (differential, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf234"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §9's filter account beside the aggregation-ordering rule; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-01` on an independently authored carrier. Two facts sit beside an existing keep rule. The clause already said a false or unknown filter result drops that row before the consumer cell is read; it did not say what becomes of the aggregate, and the neighbouring TARGET rule says the first formally unavailable selected cell makes the whole aggregate unavailable. The two positions are opposite, and one document carries both.

**A dropped row leaves the aggregate AVAILABLE, answering over the survivors.** With every row's filter cell malformed, `Sum == 0` and `NumberOfFilledFields == 0` both fire — an ordinary zero over an empty selection, not an unavailable result. A count ladder (`== 0`, `== 1`, `== 2`) brackets the survivor count exactly, so a mixed document reports one survivor against the well-formed control's two: per-row exclusion, not aggregate collapse.

**The empty-operand-as-zero rule reaches an ABSENT operand and not a formally invalid one.** An absent Number filter cell participates as `0` and the comparison decides, so `[Amt] < 5` keeps its row and the document answers exactly as the well-formed control; a malformed cell makes the conjunct non-true in BOTH comparison directions and keeps no row under either. The `> 5` / `< 5` pair is what separates the two: under `> 5` a substituted zero and a dropped row agree, so a single direction shows nothing.

**The target position obeys the opposite rule, measured on the same document.** One malformed SELECTED `Paid` cell takes the whole `< 5` ladder silent, while the `> 5` ladder on that same document selects no row at all, never reads the malformed cell, and answers an ordinary `0`.

**Consumer consequence.** An estate that routes a non-true conjunct to an unavailable aggregate diverges on every filtered aggregate over a document with one malformed filter cell; one that reduces the three-valued drop to a substituted value comparing false diverges on the absent-operand row.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.HavingNonTrueRowDiffTest` — seven documents × a nine-rule ladder on two carriers, both code-generation strategies and the interpreter. Two of the seven are the ROW-POSITION control that a defect of this project's own required: see [IF319](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if319).)*

## §9 supplement — a `Having` filter's connectives are COMMUTATIVE on validation and ORDER-SENSITIVE on computation, and both connectives short-circuit (differential, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf235"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §9's filter account with the arm asymmetry; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-03`. Validation evaluates a filter as a strong-Kleene tree, where the dominating operand wins from either side, so authored operand order is unobservable. Computation reads it left to right and aborts on the first poison it actually reaches, so authored order decides the result. Every row below is one document whose cells never change; only the spelling differs.

**Both connectives short-circuit, each on its own dominating polarity.** With a malformed `Weight` beside a present `Carrier`, `Having (FieldFilled(Carrier) Or FieldFilled(Weight))` computes and the reverse spelling clears. With the same malformed cell beside an ABSENT `Carrier`, `Having (FieldFilled(Carrier) And FieldFilled(Weight))` computes and its reverse clears. So the rule is about the ARM, not about `Or`.

**The control that separates a short-circuit from a conjunction that ignores its poison.** Filling `Carrier` leaves the conjunction nothing to dominate on, and BOTH spellings then clear.

**The validation arm on the identical models and documents is commutative at both connectives** — the malformed operand is unknown, and `T ∨ U = T` / `F ∧ U = F` hold from either side.

**Consumer consequence, and it is the load-bearing half.** Reordering a filter's operands is verdict-preserving on validation and NOT result-preserving on computation, so a normalizing or rule-refactoring transformation proved sound against validation alone is unsound for computations.

**And the obvious substitute does not work**, measured on the two spellings whose outcomes differ: the eager `formalErrorsInOperands` inventory names the malformed cell under BOTH — the one that computes `5` and the one that clears — so it records that an operand was formally invalid, never that a computation aborted, and cannot stand in as an abort predicate.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.HavingConnectiveArmDiffTest` — four spellings × two documents × both arms, from one model per spelling carrying a rule and a computation over the same authored filter; plus the operand-inventory reading above, and the two-row compute case that guards [IF319](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if319)'s compute arm.)*

## §9 supplement — a `Having` condition is the ORDINARY grammar, and its binding gate is a syntactic occurrence check over any reopened level (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf236"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §9's filter account, which said the filter must reference a *field* in a starred level; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-02`, `-04`, `-05` and the static half of `-07`. The condition inside a filter is the ordinary production, and the only refusal it draws is the general binding gate — which is about SCOPE rather than about the leaf's shape.

**Admitted inside a filter**, each measured in the position claimed for it: String equality against a literal and against another String field, `FieldFilled` and `FieldNotFilled`, Number `!=`, `And`, `Or`, a bracketed `And`/`Or` mix, and a bare outer scalar reference beside an in-scope conjunct. The group-presence leaf was measured separately ([`HavingFilterConditionLeafLawsTest`](../src/test/java/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/rulekit/validate/laws/HavingFilterConditionLeafLawsTest.java)).

**The gate, stated once: a filter must carry an UNMARKED reference into a level its operand's star reopens.** Four properties follow, each with a row that kills a rival reading. **Corrected 2026-09-05: this is ONE of two gates, and every row here was taken as the filter's sole condition, which is the column that cannot see the other one** — a reference to a repeatable level off the operand's path draws `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` and no conjunct rescues it, while everything below is rescued by any in-scope conjunct ([KF244](#kf244)). It accepts ANY reopened level, so a two-star operand's filter may bind only the outer starred one. It is CONNECTIVE-BLIND: an in-scope reference under `Or` satisfies it even though the filter can be satisfied without consulting that disjunct — an occurrence check, not a satisfiability analysis. It counts REFERENCES rather than field pointers: `CurrentRepetition(G) != CurrentRepetition($G)` is admitted although a `CurrentRepetition` operand contributes no field pointer, so a gate built over the reference expansion refuses a model the kernel admits. And a `$`-marked reference does not satisfy it, because the marker moves the reference out of the filtered level.

**The marker's own rule is about the LEVEL, and the two refusals have different codes.** A marked reference to a level the enclosing iteration BINDS is admitted; one to a level the operand's own star REOPENS draws `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`, while a filter with no unmarked in-scope reference at all draws `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD`. The pointer-free rows need the SELF-EXCLUSION topology — rule and operand at the same repeatable level — because only there is one level both reopened and enclosing-bound, which is what lets a marked and an unmarked reference to it both be legal in one condition.

**Two refused shapes are unrepresentable in this project rather than refused by it, and both erasures now rest on our OWN measurement.** `DslRenderer` parenthesizes a nested logic node whose operator differs from its parent, so the `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` mix has no rendering; and the comparison verbs are typed per value kind, so a cross-kind leaf has no method. Put to the kernel as raw condition strings, the two shapes draw `MVK_BRACKET_MISSING` and `MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON`, with the bracketed spelling admitted as the control — so the client-side erasures have a measured basis of ours rather than a peer's report.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterGrammarAndScopeLawsTest` — five row sets over one two-level model, every condition rendered from the typed builder so each row measures authorability and kernel admission at once.)*

## §9/§11 supplement — a bare outer reference on a NON-REOPENED level reads the bound coordinate, so the `$` marker is redundant there (differential, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf237"></a>

> Fold: pending — corrects §9's reading that `$` is the sole way a filter reaches an outer field; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-07`. The rule splits by LEVEL, not by scope. For a level the star REOPENS, the marker is the only way to read the captured coordinate and the unmarked reference reads the candidate's — that difference is the whole of correlation. For an unstarred ANCESTOR on the operand's own path, the candidate environment inherits the coordinate from the captured prefix, so both spellings are admitted and read the same row.

> **Corrected 2026-09-05 — that second sentence said "a level the enclosing iteration BINDS and the star does not reopen", which is one carrier wider than anything measured here.** Every row below hosts the rule at `Lines` and stars `Items` beneath it, so the level is an unstarred ancestor ON the operand's path AND enclosing-bound, and the two never came apart. On a SIBLING repeatable group the enclosing iteration binds nothing inside the filter: the unmarked reference draws `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` whether or not the rule iterates that level, and only the `$` spelling is admitted — so the marker is redundant for an ancestor and load-bearing for a sibling ([KF244](#kf244)).

**Measured on varying answers rather than on agreement alone.** A rule iterating `Lines` with an operand starring only `Items`, `Cap = 5, 0, 5`: the `== 2` and `== 0` ladders select `Lines[1]`+`Lines[3]` and `Lines[2]` respectively, and each spelling selects exactly the rows its twin does. Asserted on the message POINTERS, since a code-set assertion would pass even if the marked spelling fired on the wrong rows.

**Consumer consequence.** A normalizing consumer needs the level split: under the old reading it would either reject a legal bare outer reference or believe adding `$` is always safe — the second is wrong on a reopened level, where it silently changes which rows the filter keeps.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.RedundantOuterMarkerDiffTest`; the static admission of both spellings is `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterGrammarAndScopeLawsTest`.)*

## §9/§11 supplement — the `$` capture source is the ITERATING INSTANCE, which may be a repeatable COMPUTATION rather than a rule (differential, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf238"></a>

> Fold: pending — widens §9's `$` account from "the iterating rule" to the enclosing evaluation; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-06`. A computation whose target is a repeatable field is evaluated once per target row, and `$` binds THAT row. Read as rule-only, a reimplementation either refuses a legal per-row computed target or leaves the capture unbound — two different wrong behaviours from one narrow word.

**Exact per-row vectors, so each document refutes the reversed reading alone.** `Higher = Sum(Amount Having [Lines/Rank] > [$Lines/Rank])` answers `50, 30, 0` over ascending ranks `1, 2, 3` with amounts `10, 20, 30`, where the reversed marker predicts `0, 10, 30`; and `0, 40, 10` over the rotated ranks `3, 1, 2` with the same amounts, against `50, 0, 20`. The rotated document is the control that the answer follows the RANK rather than the row position. An unbound capture predicts no outcome on any row.

**The static half is separate and was measured first**: the per-row computed target carrying a `$`-correlated filter is admitted by `checkConsistency`, so the shape is legal rather than merely tolerated at runtime.

**The same widening reaches `CurrentRepetition`, measured 2026-09-04.** The narrow word is not specific to `$`: our own operator catalog said "the rule must iterate over that group", which is the identical rule-only reading one construct over. Measured on two computations with the identical calc `CurrentRepetition(Lines)`, differing only in where the computed target sits — a repeatable target under `Lines` is **admitted**, a root target is refused `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. So a repeatable computation instance binds `CurrentRepetition` exactly as it binds `$`. a12-kernel-lean does not hold this row (their `SG17` names it open alongside the same question); it was measured here because the catalog line is a SHIPPED surface served by `dmtool operators CurrentRepetition`, and it has been widened to "the ENCLOSING ITERATION". **Corrected 2026-09-04:** this paragraph then said "the binding condition is the enclosing iteration in both cases", which is still one source too few for the UNMARKED form — an operand's own star binds it as well ([KF241](#kf241)). The correction is narrow and does not touch the `$` half above, whose single source this round's measurement confirms.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.CorrelatedComputationCaptureDiffTest` — both vectors on both code-generation strategies and the interpreter, compared on indexed pointers so the three rows cannot collapse; `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterGrammarAndScopeLawsTest.aRepeatableComputationBindsCurrentRepetitionAsAnIteratingRuleDoes` — the `CurrentRepetition` widening with its root-target control.)*

## §6/§11 supplement — the temporal CONSTANT gate reads family, year agreement and day validity — never component sets — and all three grounds share ONE code (kernel `checkConsistency` + `compute`, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf239"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF222](#kf222)'s constant-assignment account; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-08` and extends it with a third refusal ground they had not separated.

**Not component sets.** `MM` is the one target whose components are a proper subset of a yearless date literal's, so it is the row that separates the accounts: `05.03.` and `13.07.` are both ADMITTED into it with no Base Year declared, and the store writes `03` and `07`. A component-set gate predicts both refused. Controls on the same targets: `05.03.` into `MM-dd` and `12:30:00` into `HH:mm:ss` are admitted, while `12:30:00` into `MM` (wrong family) and `05.03.2024` into `MM` (year disagreement) are refused.

**A third ground: the literal must BE a date.** Same target, same family, same year agreement, only the day-in-month varying — `29.02.` and `31.04.` into `MM-dd` are refused, `30.04.` is admitted. So the yearless leap day is refused because without a year it is not a date, and the gate is validating the day rather than special-casing February. a12-kernel-lean's entry does not carry this ground.

**All three report `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE`**, so a consumer must re-derive which rule fired from the constant/target pair; a corrective telling the author to supply a Base Year is wrong on the family and day-validity rows.

**The gate reads the same two operands on the COMPARISON carrier too.** A yearless literal against a year-free DATE field with no Base Year is admitted; a year-carrying one against the same field is refused with the same code. That matters beyond symmetry: it is the shape that exposed [IF321](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if321), since a consumer must resolve the literal there as well as at an assignment.

**A temporal OPERATION is the third carrier, and it is governed by DIFFERENT gates.** A year-free *literal* is admitted once the operation's field operand allows it: `DifferenceInDays("05.03.", "07.04.")` over two constants, and a literal reaching the operation through `AddDays`. An aggregate over two constants is refused for constant count instead (`MVK_TOO_MANY_CONST_FOR_CALC_OP`), which is not a format gate at all. So "the constant gate" is one of **five** that can refuse a temporal constant — this one, `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`, `MVK_DATE_WITH_AND_WITHOUT_YEAR`, `MVK_TOO_MANY_CONST_FOR_CALC_OP` and the `MVK_NO_CONST` below — and only this one reads year agreement.

**Corrected 2026-09-04: the operand rule is GRANULARITY, not year-bearing-ness.** This entry first said "a year-free field is refused as an operation operand outright, so the gate reads the field's format and not the constant's". Both halves were over-general, and the confound was that every row taken here used a year-free field. Measured on one model varying only the operand's declared format: `MM` is refused `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP`, **`MM-dd` is ADMITTED** against a yearless literal, and a year-carrying `dd.MM.yyyy` field against a yearless literal is refused under a *different* code, `MVK_DATE_WITH_AND_WITHOUT_YEAR` (the same field against a year-carrying literal is admitted — the control). So `MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP` is about whether the operand's granularity supports a day difference, and the constant/field year relation has its own code. Reported by a12-kernel-lean (`SPEC-2026-09-04-02`) and re-measured here rather than taken on their report. They additionally report that `DifferenceInYears`/`AddYears` refuse operands `DifferenceInDays` admits; that arm is theirs and is not measured here.

**The reference year a yearless literal borrows is the model's BASE YEAR, and this carrier is what makes it observable.** `DifferenceInDays("28.02.", "01.03.")` is 1 day in a common year and 2 in a leap year. Measured on one model varying only the `baseYear` builder call: Base Year **2024** answers 2, Base Year **2023** answers 1, and with **no Base Year declared** the kernel still resolves and answers 2. The assignment and comparison carriers cannot see any of this — the assignment stores only the components its target's format names, and the comparison's admitted shapes are year-free on both sides. It exposed [IF322](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if322).

**Corrected 2026-09-04: this entry first said "the anchor is a LEAP year", which was the confound rather than the rule.** Every row it rested on declared **no Base Year**, so "the anchor is always leap" and "the anchor is the Base Year, whose unconfigured default happens to be leap" fit the whole set identically — the constant-across-every-row failure this project's own rules name, caught by a12-kernel-lean (`SPEC-2026-09-04-01`) supplying the axis and re-measured here. The leap claim survives only as the **unconfigured default**.

**The unconfigured default's PARITY is measured; its year is not, and the direct route is closed rather than untried.** Reading the borrowed year back with `YearFromDate("05.03.")` is refused `MVK_NO_CONST` — that extractor admits no constant operand at all. Any leap year satisfies what is measured. a12-kernel-lean reports six routes refused and no weekday extractor among the 110 catalog operators, recorded there as a searched denominator rather than as unreachability.

**One qualification the admitted/refused rows do not show, because none of them declares a Base Year.** The kernel's year-agreement gate returns true unconditionally once a Base Year exists, so the year-disagreement ground above is the rule for a base-year-FREE model; every row here sits on that side of the axis, and nothing measured here speaks for the other.

**The time-side mirror is unreachable rather than unrun**: an hour-only `HH` format is refused, so no time target has components that are a proper subset of a time literal's. Measured here the refusal lands on the kernel-backed model check rather than on this project's draft builder, which writes the declaration without consulting the kernel; the derived [`TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md`](TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md) lists `HH` under *Refused* and `MM`/`MM-dd` under *Admitted*, which is the same fact from the generated side.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.TemporalConstantAdmissionGateLawsTest` — the gate rows, the comparison carrier, the two shapes our typed builder cannot author measured against the kernel directly, and a builder column covering every kernel-admitted row so an over-strict client-side refusal cannot hide; `adapter.laws.YearlessConstantMonthStoreDiffTest` — the store on both admitted year-free formats, tri-engine; `adapter.laws.YearlessConstantComparisonDiffTest` — the comparison at runtime; `adapter.laws.YearlessConstantOperationDiffTest` — the operation carrier and the leap-year anchor, tri-engine. The interpreter defects these rows exposed are [IF320](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if320), [IF321](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if321) and [IF322](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if322).)*

## §11 supplement — the two CLEAR-KINDS part ways at a PLAIN OPERAND read, poison crosses a join, and the producer's own reported state is blind to the difference (differential, both strategies, 2026-09-03) <a id="kf240"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §11's cascade read-rules from filter/precondition reads to an ordinary operand; folds into §11 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-03-09`. This repository had measured both cascade read-rules only for reads reaching INSIDE a downstream `Having` filter or a precondition's quantifiers (§11's cascade supplement, IF98). They govern a plain operand read as well, and that is the whole observable difference between the two kinds of clear.

**One four-deep diamond held fixed across producer states** — `Posted = [Base]`, `Left = [Posted]`, `Right = [Alt]`, `Total = [Left] + [Right]` — with `Right` as the liveness control on every row. Clean gives `7, 7, 5, 12`. A producer cleared by an unmet PRECONDITION, with no malformed cell anywhere, gives `Left = 0` and `Total = 5`: empty substitution. A producer cleared by a MALFORMED SOURCE clears `Left` and `Total` while `Right` still answers `5`: **poison crosses the join** rather than being substituted away, and one failing branch does not abort the plan. The absent-source leg answers `0, 0, 5, 5`, and it is what makes the first two distinguishable without appealing to the join's shape.

**The clear is visible to a dependent inside the same call.** With a stale value stored in the cleared producer, `Left` still answers `0` — on two different stale seeds, so it is the cleared state rather than a coincidence of one number. A consumer that clears at application time and lets dependents read pre-call storage passes every fresh-value row and fails exactly here.

**A bare CONSTANT operation honours a precondition**, writing when met and clearing when not, its clear read as empty by the same rule.

**The producer cannot be asked which kind it is.** Both clearing rows report `cleared=true, errored=false` on the producer's own instance, so a consumer predicting propagation from that flag is wrong on the malformed row. The channel that does separate them for a producer with NO dependents is the eager `formalErrorsInOperands` inventory: the source-invalid producer's own operand appears there and the precondition-cleared one's does not. It is an INVENTORY rather than a causal attribution — it also names operands of computations that succeeded, measured in [KF235](#kf235) on a spelling that computes a value — so the consumer's discriminator is whether the producer's own operand set intersects it, not the inventory's mere non-emptiness. The residue is a producer cleared because a COMPUTED field it read was poisoned: a computed field is outside that inventory's scope by definition, so that case stays indistinguishable.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.DependencyClearKindDiffTest` — five documents over one diamond, tri-engine, plus the producer-state and operand-inventory channels asserted directly.)*

## §9 supplement — an unmarked `CurrentRepetition` has TWO binding sources, and an operand's own star is the second (kernel `checkConsistency` + differential, both strategies, 2026-09-04) <a id="kf241"></a>

> Fold: pending — supersedes the single-source reading [KF238](#kf238) states for `CurrentRepetition`; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-04-03`, re-derived here on two carriers of our own because the sentence it corrects is a SHIPPED surface: the operator catalog served by `dmtool operators CurrentRepetition`. An **unmarked** `CurrentRepetition(G)` is bound by the enclosing iteration **or** by an operand's own star that reopens `G`; a **`$`-marked** `CurrentRepetition($G)` reads the captured environment and is bound only by the enclosing iteration. So a filter on a starred operand may carry an unmarked index even though its host does not iterate — the shape the single-source reading predicts refused.

**The marker is isolated on one host, one shape.** From a rule at the nonrepeatable `/Policy`, `Sum(the flatten of Endorsements* then Premium Having CurrentRepetition(/Policy/Endorsements) > 0) > 0` is **admitted** and the identical aggregate with `CurrentRepetition($/Policy/Endorsements)` is refused `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`. Only the marker differs.

**Three controls, each killing a different rival.** The same aggregate **unfiltered** and the same aggregate with an ordinary field leaf in its filter are both admitted from that host, so neither the star nor the filter is what the marked row refuses. And the same **unmarked** operand with no star anywhere is refused too — which is what shows the STAR does the binding rather than the marker's mere absence. Without that row, "unmarked is simply tolerated" fits every other verdict.

**The runtime half is a separate claim and was measured separately**, because admission says nothing about evaluation and this repository is exactly the compiling consumer the entry warns about. Over premiums `10, 20, 30` the filtered `Sum` for `CurrentRepetition(Endorsements) > 1` is **50** on both kernel strategies and the interpreter; the two rival readings are pinned as failing rows rather than left implicit — a filter read as always-true gives `60` (the unfiltered control's own value) and an unbound coordinate that survives no candidate gives `0`, and both are asserted not to fire.

**Extended 2026-09-04: the star binds the FILTER and not the RULE — one message, at the host's own field.** The rows above read *whether* the code appears, which is identical for a rule that fires once and one that fires per row, so the seam a12-kernel-lean's reply asked about (what a non-iterating rule DOES with a `CurrentRepetition` operand) was unmeasured while looking answered. Reading the fired-message list per engine instead of a boolean: over the same three-row list, with **two** rows surviving the filter, all three engines report exactly `["/Policy[1]/SettlementTotal"]` — one message, attached to the non-repeatable host's own error field, never one per surviving row. Two rows rather than one is what makes the row discriminating, and the pointer rather than a bare count is what separates "fires once" from "fires per row and was deduplicated". *(Locked: `adapter.laws.CurrentRepetitionOperandStarBindingDiffTest.theStarredOperandDoesNotMakeTheRuleIterate`.)*

**What our catalog said, and what it says now.** The line read "the ENCLOSING ITERATION must iterate over that group … otherwise `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`", unqualified — which predicts the admitted row refused. It had already been widened once this round from "the rule's" to "the enclosing iteration's" ([KF238](#kf238)); that widening was right and still incomplete, because it replaced one binding source with another rather than adding the second. Both the constraint and the surprise gotcha now name the two sources and the marker that selects between them.

**Which star binds — and the code, both corrected 2026-09-04 by the row this entry needed and did not have.** The sentence above says "an operand's own star that reopens `G`", and every row that established it sat on a carrier with exactly ONE starrable level relative to the operand — `/Policy` has a single repeatable subgroup and the `/Order` claim probe a single repeatable group — so "the star that reopens `G`" and "any position inside a filter" fit all of them equally. A cold review named the confound; the discriminating row was then run on the two-level `/Catalog/Lines` ▸ `/Catalog/Lines/Items` carrier, hosted at the ROOT so no enclosing iteration binds anything, with the operand starring `Lines` only. Naming `Lines` is **admitted** (which also transfers this entry's claim to a second carrier); naming `Items` — repeatable, neither starred nor iterated — is **refused**, so the narrow account holds and the broad one is refuted. **But the refusal is `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION`, not `MVK_NO_WILDCARD`** — the filter-scope gate whose meaning §9 already recorded for a FIELD reference ("why `$` exists"), which turns out to receive a group operand too. So the unbound code depends on WHY the operand is unbound, not only on where it sits: `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` outside any filter and for the marked form inside one, this code for an unmarked operand naming an unreopened level. The catalog's `constraint[1]` and `gotcha[1]` said `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` for every unbound case and are corrected; the same-leaf two-star row is the positive control that tells a binding refusal from a leaf refusal.

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.CurrentRepetitionBindingSourceLawsTest` — the five admission rows on the `/Policy` carrier; `adapter.laws.CurrentRepetitionOperandStarBindingDiffTest` — the value-exact runtime rows tri-checked across groovy-dynamic, generated Java and the interpreter; `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterGrammarAndScopeLawsTest.onlyTheStarThatReopensTheNamedGroupBindsAnUnmarkedOperand` — the three-row discriminator on the two-level carrier, which is what separates the star-over-the-named-group account from the filter-position one; and the catalog's own CI-executed claim probe `CurrentRepetition.operand-star-binds-unmarked`, which reproduces the admitted and refused pair on the independent `/Order` fixture.)*

## §9 supplement — a group-presence leaf inside a `Having` filter obeys the FIELD leaf's scope gate, marked or not (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-04) <a id="kf242"></a>

> Fold: pending — completes [KF218](#kf218)/§9's filter-scope account with the group carrier and its `$` spelling; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-04-05`, and closes a residue both estates recorded as open: their disposition on `SPEC-2026-09-03-04` states it "stays unmeasured on both sides". A **NON-REPEATABLE** out-of-scope **group** leaf as a filter's sole condition is refused `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` in **both** spellings, and one in-scope conjunct admits either. So `GroupFilled` reads the captured environment as a field reference does, and on a bound-but-not-reopened level the marker is redundant there too.

> **Corrected 2026-09-05 — that sentence said "an out-of-scope group leaf", and the word NON-REPEATABLE above is the repair.** Both carriers measured for this entry were non-repeatable subgroups (`/Order`'s `Billing`, and the `Meta` of lean's own `/TL/Outer` shape), so repeatability was constant across every row and the account fitted them all while being false one carrier over. `GroupFilled` on a repeatable SIBLING draws `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` as the sole condition **and beside an in-scope conjunct** — the presence leaf splits by the named group's repeatability exactly as a field reference does, so it obeys both gates rather than one out-of-scope rule ([KF244](#kf244), `HavingFilterIterationGateLawsTest.aGroupPresenceLeafObeysTheSameTwoGatesRatherThanOneOutOfScopeRule`).

**The marker is isolated by measuring both spellings at each position.** As the sole condition, marked and unmarked draw the *same* code — which is what shows the missing in-scope reference is the cause rather than the marker; the refusal alone would not have distinguished them. Beside `[/Order/Lines/Qty] > 1` both are admitted, with the conjunct alone as the live control. `GroupNotFilled($G)` behaves identically **in both positions** (measured 2026-09-04: refused as the sole condition, admitted beside an in-scope conjunct, marked and unmarked alike), so the answer is about the group-presence carrier and not about one operator.

**Reproduced twice, on two carriers.** The rows above are the `/Order` laws carrier; a `dmtool`-authored `/TL/Outer` model with a nonrepeatable `Meta` subgroup — lean's own shape — gives the same four verdicts through `rule check`, every one `KERNEL_CONFIRMED`.

**Our own answer to their "which do you do?" question.** This repository neither erases the marker before a scope check nor inspects it: admission is delegated whole to `checkConsistency`, and `ConditionReferences`/`Linter` treat a marked reference exactly as an unmarked one on every carrier — so both spellings already took the same path and the residue was a gap in the *account*, not in the code. What the round did change is that the marker is now **representable**: `GroupPresenceCondition` could not hold it, so the shape was unauthorable *and* — because the converter's `verifyOuterPreserved` counts source markers against rendered ones — a legal model carrying one was degraded to a verbatim read rather than converted ([API-FINDINGS 135](API-FINDINGS.md)).

*(Locked: `rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterConditionLeafLawsTest.theDollarMarkerOnTheGroupLeafIsAdmittedAndChangesNoVerdict` — the six rows plus a render assertion proving the `$` actually reaches the kernel; `adapter.laws.CorrelatedGroupPresenceReadTest` — the read path; and the catalog's CI-executed claim probe `GroupFilled.marked-leaf-in-filter`.)*

## §11 supplement — a no-value computation's REPORTED shape follows the target cell's prior state, not the ground of the no-value (differential, both strategies + interpreter, 2026-09-04) <a id="kf243"></a>

> Fold: pending — sharpens [KF240](#kf240)'s clear-kind account with the axis that decides the *reported* shape; folds into §11 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

**Corrects a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-04-04` rather than confirming it.** Their clause says a per-row target whose filtered candidate set is **empty** produces no computation outcome at all, "where a precondition-cleared or source-invalid producer is reported present and cleared". Both halves reproduce here **on the precondition ground** — the source-invalid ground is not on this axis in this entry (its own rows sat on a stale seed), so "both halves" names the reported-present-and-cleared pair rather than both grounds, which the closing scope note states and this sentence used to blur. And they are not a contrast between the two GROUNDS. A no-value outcome is reported `CLEARED` when the target cell was **stale-filled** and not reported at all when it was **absent**, whichever ground produced it. Their comparison put an unseeded empty-candidate target beside a stale cleared one, so it moved two variables and the seed is the one that decides.

**The 2×2 that separates them**, within one model and one document per cell, over a per-row String target on three rows:

| target cell | empty candidate set | unmet precondition |
|---|---|---|
| seeded (stale) | `CLEARED` | `CLEARED` |
| absent | no outcome | no outcome |

Both diagonals are measured, which is what no account of the ground can produce: seeding only the empty-candidate target reverses which ground looks like the absent one.

**Exact per-row values, so each document refutes the reversed marker reading alone.** `FirstFilledValue(the flatten of Lines* then Sku Having [Lines/Price] > [$Lines/Price])` over ascending prices `10, 30, 20` with skus `A, B, C` answers `B`, no value, `B` — the reversed reading predicts `nothing, A, A`. Descending prices `30, 20, 10` answer no value, `A`, `A` against a predicted `B, B, nothing`, and that document is also the control that the no-value row follows the ROW rather than a position, since this channel's first instance is easy to misread.

**The dependent is the half a measurement from the reporting channel alone gets wrong**, and their entry records correcting exactly that before sending. A `Length` reader answers `0` over the no-value row and is present on **every** row — including the seeded one, so it reads the outcome rather than the stale cell. Both absence shapes are therefore indistinguishable downstream and neither is poison.

**Why the first attempt at this looked like an interpreter defect, recorded because it is the trap and not the finding.** `DmInterpreter.compute` reports every computed instance by contract while the kernel's own result is its three-channel CHANGE projection, so a raw comparison shows the interpreter inventing a `CLEARED` for every unseeded no-value target — the exact shape under test. The comparison has to project first (`conformance.kernelComputeGranularity`, whose contract already stated the rule this entry measures: a cleared instance is reported only when the input had the cell filled). An altitude mismatch between two channels reads as a divergence, and it reads as one *in the direction you are already looking*.

**Stated scope.** One carrier (String), one per-row target, two grounds. The source-invalid ground of [KF240](#kf240) is not on this axis here; its own rows were taken over a stale seed, which is consistent with the account above but is not a measurement of the absent-target cell.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.EmptyCandidateSetOutcomeDiffTest` — the full 2×2 plus both value vectors and the dependent, tri-checked across groovy-dynamic, generated Java and the interpreter at kernel granularity.)*

## §9 supplement — a `Having` filter answers to TWO gates, and only one of them yields to a conjunct (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf244"></a>

> Fold: pending — supersedes the single-gate reading in [KF236](#kf236) and narrows [KF237](#kf237); folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-01` on our own carrier, and corrects two of our published statements in the process. A filter condition passes two independent checks, and the code names which one refused.

| the condition's out-of-scope reference names… | sole condition | beside a reference the operand's star reopens |
|---|---|---|
| the level the operand's own star reopens | admitted | admitted |
| a NON-repeatable group | `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` | **admitted** |
| an unstarred repeatable ANCESTOR on the operand's path | `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` | **admitted** |
| a repeatable level OFF the operand's path | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |
| that same off-path level **while the rule iterates it** | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` | `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` |
| that same off-path level under the `$` marker | `MVK_NO_ITERATION_FOR_WILDCARD` | **admitted** |
| the `$` marker with no enclosing iteration to capture | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` | `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` |

**The conjunct column is what separates them, and either column alone is consistent with one gate whose code varies.** Drop the conjunct column and the two codes read as a spelling difference; drop the repeatability column and the second gate is invisible. Our own rows had only the sole-condition column, which is why [KF236](#kf236) stated one gate.

**The enclosing rule iteration does NOT bind a filter reference — the correction to [KF237](#kf237).** That entry says a level the enclosing iteration binds and the star does not reopen admits both spellings. Every row it measured put that level on the operand's own path as an unstarred ancestor (a rule at `Lines` filtering an operand starring `Items` below it), so "on the operand's path" and "bound by the enclosing iteration" moved together and the visible half was the wrong one. Measured here on two SIBLING repeatable groups — a rule hosted at `Claims`, an operand starring `Parcels*` — the unmarked reference to `Claims` is refused whether or not the rule iterates it, and only the `$` spelling is admitted. So KF237 holds for an unstarred ancestor and not for a sibling; the marker is redundant only in the first case.

**The carrier is irrelevant, which is the second correction.** Our shipped catalog attributed `MVK_INVALID_ITERATION_IN_FILTER_CONDITION` to an *unmarked `CurrentRepetition` operand*, implying the spelling selects the code. A plain field reference draws the identical code in the identical position, and both carriers agree in all four measured positions. The gate is a property of `Having`, so the account now lives on `Having`'s catalog entry and `CurrentRepetition`'s defers to it.

**What is NOT established, stated so it is not read as measured.** Every refused row names a level that is at once off the operand's path and unbound by its star; every admitted out-of-scope row names one that is at once on that path and bound by the enclosing iteration. The cell separating those readings — an unstarred repeatable ancestor on the operand's path that nothing binds — cannot be authored: the OPERAND alone is already `MVK_NO_WILDCARD` there, with the unfiltered control confirming the refusal is the operand's and not the filter's. So "outside the operand's path" and "bound by no enclosing iteration" are extensionally equal over every legal model, and neither is claimed as the mechanism.

*(Locked: [`rulekit.validate.laws.HavingFilterIterationGateLawsTest`](../src/test/java/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/rulekit/validate/laws/HavingFilterIterationGateLawsTest.java) — four row sets, 23 rows, one model with two sibling repeatable groups. CI-executed catalog claim probes `Having.iteration-gate-yields-to-no-conjunct`, `Having.scope-gate-yields-to-any-in-scope-conjunct` and `Having.marker-needs-an-outer-coordinate` pin the three codes against the kernel from the prose that states them.)*

## §13 supplement — the rule-message `$#…$` GROUP parameter renders the named level's own repetition INDEX in the firing row (tri-engine, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf245"></a>

> Fold: pending — the runtime half of [KF214](#kf214), which measured only which arguments the position ADMITS; folds into §13 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-02` on our own carrier. An admitted group parameter renders the **1-based repetition index of the named group in the firing row**, and the constant `1` for a non-repeatable group. Both keyword shorthands render exactly as the paths they abbreviate.

**The discriminating document, because the obvious one cannot separate the accounts.** A per-row rule over three `/Claim/Lines` rows, gated to fire on rows **2 and 3** and stay silent on row 1: the messages read `own=[2]` and `own=[3]`. A *firing-ordinal* account predicts `1` and `2`; a *row-count* account predicts `3` and `3`. On any document whose rule fires from row 1, or fires once, all three accounts agree — so the gap in the fixture carries the finding, not the number of rows.

`root=[1]` is the non-repeatable arm in the same message, and `rule=`/`top=` are `$#RuleGroup$`/`$#RootGroup$` rendering identically to the absolute paths they abbreviate. A `$Marker$` parameter rides in the same message as a within-message control, rendering the FIELD's name — so the two positions are separated by their output rather than by their grammar, and a silent fallback to name-rendering in the group position would be visible.

**Each admitted argument reads the coordinate at its OWN level — the row the single-level fixture above cannot carry** (added 2026-09-05). On one repeatable level every non-root argument resolves to the same coordinate, so "the named group's own row index" and "the firing row's index whatever is named" are indistinguishable there. A second fixture stacks two repeatable levels under a **repeatable root** and fires at consignment 2, box 3, items 2 and 4: one message reads `item=[4] box=[3] cons=[2]`, three distinct integers, and `top=[2]` is `$#RootGroup$` on a repeatable root — the arm where "the chain root's index" and the constant `1` finally separate. The per-segment quote escape renders identically to the bare spelling (`$#/'Consignment'/'Boxes'$` → `3`), which is the runtime half of this entry's admission-side quoting row.

**The GERMAN shorthands render the same two coordinates their English twins do** (added 2026-09-05). On a `de_DE`-condition model whose rule sits at `/Lieferung/Posten` under a **repeatable root**, one message reads `eigen=[3] regel=[3] wurzel=[2]` for the third item of the second delivery — `$#RegelKontext$` the rule group's row and `$#LfdNr$` the chain root's. Both kernel strategies and the interpreter agree. The root repeats on purpose: on a non-repeatable one `wurzel=` is the constant `1` and the row would say nothing about which reading is right. The condition is rendered by `DslRenderer(ConditionLanguage.DE)` rather than hand-spelled, so the German keywords are the renderer's own.

**Corrected 2026-09-05 — the interpreter now implements the construct.** The first version of this entry recorded, correctly at the time, that it passed `$#…$` through verbatim; that was `IG148`, shipped the same day as [IF323](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if323), and every row above now agrees on all three engines. *(Also corrected the same day: this paragraph first said the German arm was locked on the interpreter alone "because no kernel runtime fixture in this estate carries a `de_DE` condition language". That was true when written and stopped being true within the hour — `RuntimeLaws.withRuleMessages` takes a raw condition, so the German model needed no new machinery. Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because "our fixtures do not carry X" is an instrument claim and this one was one command from being false.)*

*(Locked: [`adapter.laws.RuleMessageGroupParameterDiffTest`](../adapter/src/test/kotlin/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/adapter/laws/RuleMessageGroupParameterDiffTest.kt) — all three fixtures, tri-engine; `RuntimeLaws.errorTextsOf` was added because `errorTextOf` takes the FIRST message, which silently collapses the rows this finding is about. `interpreter … RuleMessageGroupParameterRenderTest` — the two shorthands in both condition languages on JVM and JS, plus the other language's spelling surviving as its own token, which no kernel fixture can carry because the kernel refuses that template.)*

## §13 supplement — a COMPUTATION's declared message is rendered by the rule the kernel generates for it, group parameter and all (tri-engine, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf246"></a>

> Fold: pending — the third carrier of the parameter surface opened by [KF198](#kf198) and [KF245](#kf245); fold all three into §13's interpolation account in one pass.

Every computation must declare an `errorMessage` (`MVK_ERROR_MESSAGE_MISSING`), and the kernel auto-generates one validation rule per computation that carries it. So this text sits on the ordinary `validateFull` output of any model with a computation, and it is a **third owner** of the parameter grammar beside a stored rule and a field-owned message.

**The parameter terminal bundle follows the owning DECLARATION, not the rule kind.** Reported as a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-06` for admission; measured here on the render side, which they explicitly did not claim. A computation at a repeatable `/Invoice/Lines` whose message reads `row=[$#RuleGroup$] qty=[$Qty.value$]`, over a document whose second row disagrees with the computed value, renders `row=[2] qty=[3]` on both kernel strategies. The group shorthand resolves against the generated rule exactly as it would in a hand-written one.

**The field parameter rides along as the discriminating control.** Without it, an engine that rendered no text at all for this carrier and an engine that rendered text but dropped the group token produce the same visible symptom — an empty or half-empty message — and only the field position separates them. It earned that role immediately: this interpreter rendered the message as the **empty string**, because its loader never read a computation's `errorMessage` ([IF324](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if324)), and the control is what showed the defect was one layer below the group parameter rather than in it.

*(Locked: [`adapter.laws.ComputationMessageDiffTest`](../adapter/src/test/kotlin/io/github/mbackschat/a12/dm/adapter/laws/ComputationMessageDiffTest.kt) — Groovy-dynamic, generated Java and the interpreter, on a computation authored through the typed `EditSession`/`Computation.Builder` surface rather than injected as JSON, so the row also witnesses that our own authoring path carries the message through.)*

## §6 supplement — a YEARLESS stored day is bounded by its month's length in the DECLARED Base Year (`validateFull`, both strategies, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf247"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §6's incomplete-format account beside [KF239](#kf239)'s admission gate; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-12` on an independently authored carrier, measured here rather than cited: their rows are their observation, and this repository now holds its own. A `MM-dd` DATE cell holding `02-29` is `datumFormatFalsch` under a declared Base Year of **2023**, admitted under **2024**, and admitted when **no** Base Year is declared at all. So the year the model anchors to is what bounds the day, not February's greatest possible length.

**The undeclared configuration is the separator, and it is why the rule is about the anchor's leapness rather than about declaring a Base Year.** A base-year-free model behaves exactly like the leap case — because the anchor it falls back to is itself a leap year — so a reading of "declaring a Base Year tightens the bound" is refuted by the row that declares none. **The century pair separates it from a `year % 4` test**, which agrees on 2023/2024 and gets 1900 wrong: 1900 is refused and 2000 admitted, so the bound is the full Gregorian rule. February is the only month whose two candidate bounds differ, so one witness settles it; `02-28` and an ordinary March day cross under all five configurations, and `02-30` is refused even under a leap anchor, which is what keeps "admitted" from meaning "unchecked".

**This estate already implemented it, and the interesting part is that our LOCK stated the fact too broadly.** All three of our paths — the two `AutoChecks` check paths and `Document`'s store/read — pass `model.baseYear ?: 2000` into `completeFragmentToIso`, which bounds the day with `daysInMonth(y, mo)` against that anchor, so every row above was already correct and is now measured. But `interpreter … TemporalDeclaredFormatFormalTest`'s grid pins `MM-dd` + `02-29` as **admitted** with no base year in its `ModelDef` at all, so that row holds *because* the fallback anchor happens to be leap and nothing in the test said so. Every row in that grid shares the one configuration — the "one CONSTANT across every row you hold" confound, with the fixture supplying the constant. The row is not wrong; it was unconditional where the fact is conditional, and the axis it was missing is the one a12-kernel-lean's entry supplies.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.YearlessDayBoundBaseYearDiffTest` — five Base Year configurations over one document and one declaration, tri-engine, with the model bytes asserted to actually carry (and in the undeclared row, to lack) the base year, plus the crossing controls and the leap-anchor `02-30` refusal.)*

## §6 supplement — the COMPARISON-admission gate partitions temporal operands by declared FORMAT, on both kinds (kernel `checkConsistency` + tri-engine runtime, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf248"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends [KF211](#kf211)'s classifier rule to the comparison gate; folds into §6 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-13`. [KF211](#kf211) established that a temporal field's declared format, never its kind, selects its formal check and its value decoder, on the complete 8-format × 3-kind grid. The operand family at the **comparison** gate follows the same rule: a clock-declared DATE compares with a clock and draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` against a date, while a date-declared TIME does the reverse.

**Why this was not already covered, which is the methodological point.** `adapter.laws.TemporalDeclaredFormatGateDiffTest` does measure the comparison gate — but on one arm (a date-declared TIME against a date-declared DATE) plus the ordinary clock-versus-date refusal as its control, and its model declares no clock-formatted DATE at all. The mirror was therefore *inherited* from the classifier rule rather than measured, and a classifier and an admission gate are different gates: that is a scope transfer, the reuse needing no new branch and so prompting no question. Measuring it took one model.

**The grid is a within-model 2×2 and every kind appears on both sides of both outcomes**, which is what rules out "DATE is the permissive kind" or "TIME is" and leaves the format; one direction alone would not have. Both admitted cross-kind arms were also RUN on all three engines, firing on equal operands and silent on unequal ones — an admission verdict cannot see a silent suppression, which is precisely the shape of the defect [IF314](INTERPRETER-FINDINGS.md#if314) fixed in this area.

**Our own surfaces already honour it, and one of them is the reason the typed API can express these conditions at all.** `BoundModel.requireTemporalShape` admits a handle when the declared format's shape matches, not only when the kind does, so `m.time(<clock-declared DATE>)` yields a time handle; without that the two admitted rows would be unauthorable through the typed surface and would read as "not a thing" rather than as admitted — the type-level-erasure failure mode. **Extended 2026-09-05 to the DATE_TIME family, which had been an explicit gap on BOTH sides.** a12-kernel-lean's entry limited itself to the DATE/TIME pair under equality and recorded the DateTime family's cross-kind comparison as untested; so did this entry, and so did four rounds of the exchange around it — each side declining to inherit the other's basis across a family boundary, correctly, since KF211's 12 × 3 grid reaches a DATE_TIME *declaration* only for the CLASSIFIER. Measured now on the same 2×2 shape one family over: a **stamp-declared DATE** compares with a stamp and draws `MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_TO_DATE` against a date, a **date-declared DATE_TIME** does the reverse, the two ordinary fields refuse each other, and both admitted arms fire tri-engine on equal operands and are silent on unequal ones. So the rule is the declared format's across all three date-bearing kinds, with each kind on both sides of both outcomes in every family.

*(Locked: `adapter.laws.CrossKindTemporalComparisonGateDiffTest` — the 2×2 admission table plus the ordinary-pair refusal and both same-family controls, the model bytes asserted to carry the contradicting declarations, and the two admitted arms run tri-engine on firing and non-firing documents.)*

## §9 supplement — an extremum's operand-family refusal names the class its FIRST operand fixed (kernel `checkConsistency`, 2026-09-05) <a id="kf249"></a>

> Fold: pending — extends §9's aggregate operand-admission account; folds into §9 on the next canonical KERNEL-SEMANTICS pass.

Confirms a12-kernel-lean's `SPEC-2026-09-05-11` on an independently authored carrier. The same two operands draw **`MVK_DATE_AND_NONDATE`** behind a temporal leader and **`MVK_NOT_SORTABLE`** behind a numeric one, so the reported code names the class the first operand fixed rather than the offender's — and an author who reorders the list to "fix" it merely changes which code they get.

**Enumerated across the family rather than sampled, because the two spellings are different operators.** `MinValue`/`MaxValue` take a bare field list and `Min`/`Max` take bracketed value expressions; all four behave identically here, and the homogeneous controls (two dates, two numbers) are admitted in both forms, which is what keeps the refusals attributable to the family mix rather than to operand count.
